reference_use.conclusion: The pinned SimonGMT library has the linear co-area formula, the injective, weighted and noninjective Lipschitz area formulas, null critical images, Rademacher, Lusin, the C¹ Whitney extension and the upper integral. It has no nonlinear co-area formula, no C¹ approximation theorem (Simon 2.1.5), no Eilenberg inequality (2.1.9), no Lemma 1.2 'only if', no tangential gradient of Lipschitz functions on rectifiable sets and no slicing. Mathlib supplies Egorov, Lebesgue differentiation, integration by parts for Lipschitz functions, change of variables, the inverse function theorem and the μHE normalisation. No DAG node proving the co-area formula or slicing is accepted. The closest node, dor_lmb_slicing_lipschitz, is the same theorem for open U; it is speculative, and its decomposition was reviewed and accepted with three children. So the needed results become nine new children, with the unique prefix dtc_bc_lc_sl_. Three accepted declarations are reused with identical frozen types: cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmcs_cd_defect_identity and cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing. All 12 types pass validate_lean_statement and elaborate in the comparator's contract-mode challenge modules. A Lean assembly derives the exact frozen type of dtc_bc_lc_slice from slice_family, slice_identity, im_calculus and dtc_mass_eq_measure, with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

rationale:
Split into 12 children: nine new lemmas (prefix dtc_bc_lc_sl_) and three comparator-accepted declarations, reused with their exact frozen types.

Why split. The supplied proof cites four groups of results without proof:
- the co-area lemma 4.1, through Simon Ch. 3: 1.6, 2.1, 2.8–2.10, Remark 1.3;
- through those, Ch. 2: 1.5 (C¹ approximation), 1.9 (Eilenberg) and 6.3–6.6 (C¹ co-area, Sard-type);
- the mollification and weak-convergence step (1) of 4.5(2);
- the "countable dense set of ω".
None of these is in the pinned SimonGMT library or accepted in the DAG. The library has the linear co-area formula, the Lipschitz area formula, Rademacher, Lusin and the C¹ Whitney extension. It has no nonlinear co-area formula, no C¹ approximation theorem, no Eilenberg inequality, no Lemma 1.2 "only if" and no slicing.
This node is at depth 4 of a depth-6 DAG, so each child here can be decomposed once more, into leaves. The analogous node dor_lmb_slicing_lipschitz (depth 3) was split into three children; its slice_family child still contains all of the above and has two levels left. Here only one level is left, so the split goes one level deeper into Simon's printed structure. Each child is a named result of Simon with its own complete proof, copied from the printed text where one exists.

Children (supplied-proof step → child):
1. c1_approx — Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.5, printed proof. Used by chart_pieces.
2. eilenberg — Ch. 2, Thm 1.9 with m = 1, printed proof. Measurable majorant of t ↦ Hⁿ(A∩f⁻¹(t)) with integral ≤ C·L·H^{n+1}(A). Used for critical points (chart_coarea) and for the null part of M (coarea).
3. c1_tangent — the C¹ sentence in the proof of Ch. 3, 1.6 "⇒": an embedded C¹ disk has its classical tangent plane as approximate tangent plane.
4. chart_pieces — Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 "only if", Remarks 1.3 and 1.5(2), and the C¹ approximation of f in the proof of 2.4. Output: disjoint C¹-chart pieces ψ_j(Y_j) covering M up to a null set, with f∘ψ_j = F_j ∈ C¹ on Y_j and T_{ψ_j y}M = Dψ_j(y)ℝ^{n+1}. Errata applied: "F_j(ℝⁿ)" for "graph F_j", Lⁿ in the choice of G_ij, and "submanifold of ℝ^{n+ℓ}".
5. chart_coarea — Ch. 2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.6 on one chart. Simon prints no proof (he cites Federer), so the standard proof is given: implicit-function straightening, Fubini and the area formula; the critical set is handled by eilenberg.

subproblems.title: C¹ approximation of a Lipschitz function off a set of small measure (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0 and let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be K-Lipschitz (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume). Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a C¹ function g : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ContDiff ℝ 1 g) such that Lⁿ({x : f(x) ≠ g(x) or Df(x) ≠ Dg(x)}) < ε, where Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x (which is 0 at points where f is not differentiable) and likewise for g.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → ℝ) (K : NNReal), LipschitzWith K f → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {x | f x ≠ g x ∨ fderiv ℝ f x ≠ fderiv ℝ g x} < ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (C¹ Approximation Theorem) and its printed proof (chapter-02.txt lines 165–268, printed pp. 42–44). Whitney's extension theorem 1.6 is available as SimonGMT `exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney`; its hypothesis 1.6(*) is the structure `HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A h D` (h and D continuous on A, and for every compact K' ⊆ A and η > 0 there is δ > 0 with |h(y) − h(x) − D(x)(y − x)| ≤ η|y − x| for x ∈ K', y ∈ A, |x − y| < δ). The printed proof is copied. The details it leaves implicit are written out: Lusin's and Egorov's theorems for the infinite measure Lⁿ (via bounded shells), measurability of the remainder suprema, and closedness of the final set. This theorem is used by the sibling chart_pieces, as Simon uses it in Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and in the proof of 2.4.

Notation. Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ. Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x. |·| is the Euclidean norm and ‖λ‖ the operator norm of a linear functional λ. For j ≥ 1 let S_j := {x : j − 1 ≤ |x| < j}. The S_j are bounded Borel sets partitioning ℝⁿ, and a bounded set meets only finitely many of the closed shells S̄_j ⊆ {j − 1 ≤ |x| ≤ j}.

1. Reductions. It suffices to treat ε < ∞: a g that works for min{ε, 1} works for ε. If n = 0, then ℝⁿ is a point and g := f works (a constant function is C¹ and the set in question is empty). Fix n ≥ 1 and ε ∈ (0, ∞).

2. Rademacher (Simon 1.4; SimonGMT `rademacher_ae_differentiableAt`, Mathlib `LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt`). The set B of points where f is differentiable is Borel (Mathlib `measurableSet_of_differentiableAt`) and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) = 0. The map x ↦ Df(x) is Borel (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`), and ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ K for every x.

3. Lusin (Simon 1.17; SimonGMT `IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.exists_isClosed_continuousOn`). Its hypotheses hold for the Lebesgue outer measure (volume.toOuterMeasure), which is Borel regular (every set has a measurable superset of equal measure, Mathlib `MeasureTheory.exists_measurable_superset`), and in ℝⁿ closed sets are G_δ (ClosedSetsAreGDelta). Fix j. Apply it, on the finite-measure Borel set S_j ∩ B, to each of the n real coordinate functions x ↦ Df(x)(e_i), with tolerance ε2^{−j−2}/n each, and intersect the n closed sets obtained. This gives a closed C_j ⊆ S_j ∩ B with Lⁿ((S_j ∩ B) ∖ C_j) < ε2^{−j−2} and Df|_{C_j} continuous (all coordinates are continuous on C_j). Put C := ⋃_j C_j.
 - C is closed and Df|_C is continuous. Since C_j ⊆ S̄_j, every point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many C_j. A union of a locally finite family of closed sets is closed, and a map that is continuous on each of finitely many closed sets is continuous on their union.
 - C ⊆ B, and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) + Σ_j Lⁿ((S_j ∩ B) ∖ C_j) < ε/4.

4. Remainders (the function R of 1.6(*)). For x, y ∈ C with x ≠ y put R(x, y) := (f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x))/|y − x|. Then |R(x, y)| ≤ 2K. For k ≥ 1 and x ∈ C put ρ_k(x) := sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k}, with sup ∅ := 0.
 - Since f is differentiable at every x ∈ C ⊆ B, ρ_k(x) decreases to 0 as k → ∞, for every x ∈ C. This is Simon's "lim_{y→x, y∈C} R(x, y) = 0 for all x ∈ C".
 - Each ρ_k is Borel on C. Let D ⊆ C be countable and dense in C. For fixed x, y ↦ R(x, y) is continuous on C ∖ {x}. Every y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < 1/k is a limit of points of D with the same property, because that condition is open in y. Hence ρ_k(x) = sup_{y∈D} |R(x, y)|·1_{0<|y−x|<1/k}. Each term is Borel in x ∈ C, because f is continuous and Df|_C is continuous; a countable supremum of Borel functions is Borel.

5. Egorov (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto`, applied on the finite-measure sets C ∩ S_j).
 - For each j there is a measurable A_j ⊆ C ∩ S_j with Lⁿ((C ∩ S_j) ∖ A_j) < ε2^{−j−2} such that ρ_k → 0 uniformly on A_j. Put A₀ := ⋃_j A_j. Then Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) < ε/4, and ρ_k → 0 uniformly on A₀ ∩ {|x| ≤ R} for every R, since this set meets only finitely many A_j.
 - By inner regularity of Lⁿ choose closed F_j ⊆ A_j with Lⁿ(A_j ∖ F_j) < ε2^{−j−2}, and put A := ⋃_j F_j. A is closed, since the F_j ⊆ S̄_j form a locally finite family. Moreover A ⊆ A₀ ⊆ C, and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) + Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) + Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) < 3ε/4 < ε. This is Simon's closed set A with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε.

6. Whitney's hypothesis 1.6(*). Put h := f and D(x) := Df(x).
 - h is continuous, and D is continuous on A ⊆ C (step 3).
 - Let K' ⊆ A be compact and η > 0. Then K' ⊆ {|x| ≤ R} for some R, so by step 5 there is k with ρ_k ≤ η on K'. Put δ := 1/k. For x ∈ K' and y ∈ A with 0 < |x − y| < δ: |h(y) − h(x) − D(x)(y − x)| = |R(x, y)|·|y − x| ≤ ρ_k(x)|y − x| ≤ η|y − x|. The case y = x is trivial.
 Hence HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A h D holds.

7. Whitney's theorem (Simon 1.6; SimonGMT `exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney`, A closed). There is g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ 1 g, g = f on A, and HasFDerivAt g (Df(a)) a for every a ∈ A, so Dg(a) = Df(a) on A.

8. Conclusion. If x ∈ A, then f(x) = g(x) and Df(x) = Dg(x). So {x : f(x) ≠ g(x) ∨ Df(x) ≠ Dg(x)} ⊆ ℝⁿ ∖ A, which has Lebesgue measure < ε by step 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: Rademacher: f is differentiable off an Lⁿ-null Borel set B, and Df is Borel.
Lusin on bounded shells: a closed C ⊆ B with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖C) < ε/4 and Df|_C continuous.
The Taylor remainder suprema ρ_k(x) on C are Borel and decrease to 0.
Egorov on bounded shells and inner regularity: a closed A ⊆ C with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖A) < ε and ρ_k → 0 uniformly on bounded subsets of A, i.e. Whitney's condition 1.6(*).
Whitney's C¹ extension (SimonGMT exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney) gives g ∈ C¹ with g = f and Dg = Df on A.

subproblems.title: Eilenberg's inequality for the level sets of a Lipschitz function (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.9 with m = 1)
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ there is a constant C ∈ [0, ∞) (depending only on n) with the following property. Let P ∈ ℕ, let A ⊆ ℝ^P be any set (not necessarily measurable), let L ≥ 0 and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz on A (LipschitzOnWith L f A). Then there is a Borel function φ : ℝ → [0, ∞] with Hⁿ(A ∩ f⁻¹(t)) ≤ φ(t) for every t ∈ ℝ and ∫_ℝ φ dL¹ ≤ C·L·H^{n+1}(A), where Hᵏ = μHE[k] on ℝ^P (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure). In Simon's language: the upper integral of t ↦ Hⁿ(A ∩ f⁻¹(t)) is at most C·L·H^{n+1}(A).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ C : NNReal, ∀ (P : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), LipschitzOnWith L f A → ∃ φ : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable φ ∧ (∀ t, μHE[n] (A ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}) ≤ φ t) ∧ ∫⁻ t, φ t ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * (L : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[n + 1] A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.9 and Remark 1.10 (chapter-02.txt lines 330–410, printed pp. 45–46), case m = 1, k = n, X = ℝ^P. The printed proof is copied. In dimension m = 1 the isodiametric inequality used there becomes the elementary bound L¹(S) ≤ diam S for S ⊆ ℝ (Mathlib `Real.volume_le_diam`). The upper integral of Remark 1.10 is made explicit by the measurable majorant φ. The measurability of t ↦ Hⁿ(A ∩ f⁻¹(t)), left as an exercise in the source, is not claimed and not needed. The proof works with Mathlib's unnormalised Hausdorff measure μH[d] and converts to μHE at the end. This theorem is used by the siblings chart_coarea (critical points) and coarea (the null part of a rectifiable set).

Notation. For d ≥ 0, δ > 0 and S ⊆ ℝ^P let μH[d]_δ(S) := inf Σ_i ⨆_{C_i ≠ ∅} (diam C_i)^d, the infimum over countable covers (C_i) of S with diam C_i ≤ δ. By Mathlib `hausdorffMeasure_apply`, μH[d](S) = sup_{δ>0} μH[d]_δ(S), and μH[d]_δ(S) increases as δ decreases. Let c_d := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on Euclid d, μH[d]) ∈ (0, ∞). It is nonzero by Mathlib `addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`, and μHE[d] = c_d·μH[d] (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`); c_d does not depend on P. Put C := c_n/c_{n+1}.

1. Extension. By McShane (Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`) there is f̃ : ℝ^P → ℝ, L-Lipschitz on ℝ^P, with f̃ = f on A. Since A ∩ f⁻¹(t) = A ∩ f̃⁻¹(t) for every t, we may assume that f is L-Lipschitz on ℝ^P.

2. Trivial cases.
 - If L = 0, then f is constant, say f ≡ c, and A ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ∅ for t ≠ c. Take φ := ∞·1_{{c}}: it is Borel, dominates, and ∫φ = ∞·L¹({c}) = 0 = C·0·H^{n+1}(A) (in [0, ∞], 0·∞ = 0).
 - If L > 0 and μH[n+1](A) = ∞, take φ ≡ ∞. This is allowed: C = c_n/c_{n+1} is finite and > 0 (c_n ≠ 0 and c_{n+1} ≠ 0), and μHE[n+1](A) = c_{n+1}·μH[n+1](A) = ∞, so the right side C·L·μHE[n+1](A) is ∞.
 So assume L > 0 and μH[n+1](A) < ∞.

3. Covers (Simon's sets C_ij). For k ≥ 1 put δ_k := 2^{−k}. Since μH[n+1]_{δ_k}(A) ≤ μH[n+1](A) < ∞, choose sets C_{k,i} (i ∈ ℕ) covering A with diam C_{k,i} ≤ δ_k and Σ_i ⨆_{C_{k,i}≠∅}(diam C_{k,i})^{n+1} ≤ μH[n+1](A) + 2^{−k}. Replacing each C_{k,i} by its closure keeps the cover and the diameters, so assume every C_{k,i} is closed. Let I_k := {i : C_{k,i} ≠ ∅}.

4. Simon's simple functions g_i. Put φ_k(t) := Σ_{i∈I_k} (diam C_{k,i})^n·1_{f(C_{k,i})}(t).
 - Each f(C_{k,i}) is σ-compact, hence Borel: C_{k,i} is closed in ℝ^P, hence a countable union of compact sets, and f is continuous. So φ_k is Borel.
 - L¹(f(C_{k,i})) ≤ diam f(C_{k,i}) ≤ L·diam C_{k,i} (`Real.volume_le_diam` and the Lipschitz bound). By monotone convergence, ∫φ_k ≤ L·Σ_{i∈I_k} (diam C_{k,i})^{n+1} ≤ L(μH[n+1](A) + 2^{−k}).

5. Pointwise bound (Simon's (2)). Fix t. The sets C_{k,i} ∩ A ∩ f⁻¹(t), i ∈ ℕ, cover A ∩ f⁻¹(t) and have diameter ≤ δ_k. If C_{k,i} ∩ A ∩ f⁻¹(t) ≠ ∅, then t ∈ f(C_{k,i}) and diam(C_{k,i} ∩ A ∩ f⁻¹(t)) ≤ diam C_{k,i}. Hence μH[n]_{δ_k}(A ∩ f⁻¹(t)) ≤ Σ_i ⨆_{C_{k,i}∩A∩f⁻¹(t)≠∅} (diam C_{k,i})^n ≤ φ_k(t). This also holds for n = 0, because the terms with empty intersection contribute 0.

6. Passage to the limit. Put φ⁰ := liminf_k φ_k, a Borel function.
 - For every t, μH[n](A ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = lim_k μH[n]_{δ_k}(A ∩ f⁻¹(t)) ≤ liminf_k φ_k(t) = φ⁰(t). The limit exists because the sequence is increasing in k with supremum μH[n].
 - By Fatou's lemma, ∫φ⁰ ≤ liminf_k ∫φ_k ≤ L·μH[n+1](A).

7. Normalisation. Put φ := c_n·φ⁰ (Borel). Then μHE[n](A ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = c_n·μH[n](A ∩ f⁻¹(t)) ≤ φ(t) for every t. Also ∫φ ≤ c_n·L·μH[n+1](A) = (c_n/c_{n+1})·L·μHE[n+1](A) = C·L·μHE[n+1](A). The constant C depends only on n. ∎
proof_key_steps: Extend f to an L-Lipschitz function on ℝ^P (McShane) and dispose of L = 0 and H^{n+1}(A) = ∞.
Choose closed δ_k-covers (C_{k,i}) of A with Σ diam^{n+1} ≤ μH[n+1](A) + 2^{−k}.
φ_k := Σ_i (diam C_{k,i})^n 1_{f(C_{k,i})} is Borel, dominates the δ_k-content of A ∩ f⁻¹(t), and has ∫φ_k ≤ L Σ diam^{n+1} since L¹(f(C)) ≤ L diam C.
φ⁰ := liminf φ_k dominates μH[n](A ∩ f⁻¹(t)); Fatou gives ∫φ⁰ ≤ L μH[n+1](A); rescale by the μHE normalising constants.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent plane of an embedded C¹ disk (Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒")
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^d open, c ∈ ℝ^d and r ∈ ℝ with closedBall(c, r) ⊆ U, and let g : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be C¹ on U (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U), injective on closedBall(c, r), with Dg(z) = fderiv ℝ g z injective for every z ∈ closedBall(c, r). Then for every z ∈ ball(c, r), the set S := g(closedBall(c, r)) has approximate tangent space Dg(z)(ℝ^d) at g(z) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d S (g z) (range Dg(z))): dim Dg(z)(ℝ^d) = d and ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(S)} φ dH^d → ∫_{Dg(z)(ℝ^d)} φ dH^d as s ↓ 0 for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,s}(y) = s⁻¹(y − x) and H^d = μHE[d].

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 100–135, printed p. 71): "since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{T_xN_j} f dHⁿ". This child states that sentence for a C¹ embedded disk and supplies its proof, which the source omits: change of variables by the area formula, then dominated convergence. The siblings chart_pieces (the sets ψ_j(B̄)) and chart_coarea (the level sets inside a chart) use it.

Notation. B̄ := closedBall(c, r) (if r < 0 there is nothing to prove). z ∈ ball(c, r) is fixed. Q := Dg(z)(ℝ^d). H^d := μHE[d]; on ℝ^d it is Lebesgue measure L^d (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). η_{x,s} = SimonGMT blowUpMap x s. For a linear map A : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, J(A) := √det(A*A) = normDet A ≥ 0.

1. dim Q = d. Dg(z) is injective, so Q = Dg(z)(ℝ^d) is d-dimensional (rank–nullity).

2. Lipschitz bounds on B̄.
 - Upper: Dg is continuous on the compact B̄ ⊆ U, so Λ := sup_{B̄}‖Dg‖ < ∞ and J_max := sup_{B̄} J(Dg) < ∞. B̄ is convex, so |g(a) − g(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b| for a, b ∈ B̄.
 - Lower: there is m > 0 with |g(a) − g(b)| ≥ m|a − b| for a, b ∈ B̄. Otherwise there are a_k ≠ b_k in B̄ with |g(a_k) − g(b_k)| < k⁻¹|a_k − b_k|. By compactness, pass to a subsequence with a_k → a, b_k → b, and e_k := (a_k − b_k)/|a_k − b_k| → e with |e| = 1.
  If a ≠ b, continuity gives g(a) = g(b), contradicting injectivity on B̄.
  If a = b, write g(a_k) − g(b_k) = ∫₀¹ Dg(b_k + τ(a_k − b_k))(a_k − b_k) dτ (the segment lies in the convex B̄ ⊆ U). Dividing by |a_k − b_k| and using continuity of Dg at a gives |Dg(a)e| = lim_k |g(a_k) − g(b_k)|/|a_k − b_k| = 0, contradicting injectivity of Dg(a).

3. Change of variables. Fix φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with support in closedBall(0, R), and s > 0. Put G_s(u) := s⁻¹(g(z + su) − g(z)) and B_s := {u : z + su ∈ B̄}, a closed convex set.
 - η_{g(z),s}(S) = G_s(B_s).
 - G_s is injective on B_s and has derivative DG_s(u) = Dg(z + su), which is injective for u ∈ B_s.
 - The weighted injective area formula with injective derivative (SimonGMT `weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative`, Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean, applied to φ⁺ and φ⁻; G_s is differentiable at every u ∈ B_s because z + su ∈ B̄ ⊆ U) gives
  ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(S)} φ dH^d = ∫_{ℝ^d} 1_{B_s}(u)·φ(G_s(u))·J(Dg(z + su)) du.
  The indicator matters: outside B_s the point z + su may lie outside U, where G_s and Dg carry no information. The integrand is measurable, since B_s is closed and G_s, Dg(z + s·) are continuous on B_s.
  Both sides are finite, because φ is bounded with compact support and J ≤ J_max.

4. Domination. By step 2, |G_s(u)| ≥ m|u| for u ∈ B_s, so φ(G_s(u)) ≠ 0 implies |u| ≤ R/m. Hence the integrand in step 3 is bounded by (sup|φ|)·J_max·1_{|u|≤R/m}. This bound is integrable and independent of s.

5. Pointwise limit as s ↓ 0. Fix u.
 - Since z ∈ ball(c, r), z + su ∈ B̄ for all small s, so 1_{B_s}(u) = 1 eventually.
 - G_s(u) → Dg(z)u, by differentiability of g at z.
 - J(Dg(z + su)) → J(Dg(z)), by continuity of Dg and of J.
 - φ is continuous.
 So the integrand 1_{B_s}(u)·φ(G_s(u))·J(Dg(z + su)) converges to φ(Dg(z)u)·J(Dg(z)).

6. Dominated convergence. The filter s ↓ 0 (𝓝[>] 0) is countably generated. Hence ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(S)} φ dH^d → ∫_{ℝ^d} φ(Dg(z)u)·J(Dg(z)) du.

7. Linear area formula. The weighted linear area formula (SimonGMT `weighted_linear_area_formula`, Chapter02/AreaLinearWeighted.lean, applied to φ⁺ and φ⁻) for the injective linear map Dg(z), whose image is Q, gives ∫_{ℝ^d} φ(Dg(z)u)·J(Dg(z)) du = ∫_Q φ dH^d.

8. Conclusion. With step 1, for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(S)} φ dH^d → ∫_Q φ dH^d as s ↓ 0. This is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d S (g z) Q, and Q = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ g z). ∎
proof_key_steps: dim Dg(z)(ℝ^d) = d, and g is bi-Lipschitz on the closed ball (compactness, injectivity of g and of Dg).
Rescale: η_{g(z),s}(S) = G_s(B_s) with G_s(u) = s⁻¹(g(z+su) − g(z)); the injective area formula turns ∫_{η(S)} φ into ∫_{B_s} φ(G_s(u)) J(Dg(z+su)) du.
The lower Lipschitz bound confines the integrand to |u| ≤ R/m; dominated convergence as s ↓ 0 gives ∫ φ(Dg(z)u) J(Dg(z)) du = ∫_{Dg(z)ℝ^d} φ dH^d.

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 ("only if" part, printed proof), Remark 1.3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 1–135, printed pp. 69–72). Also the sentence in the proof of Ch. 3, 2.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 375–380): "We may suppose (decomposing Hⁿ-almost all M_j as a countable union if necessary and using the C¹ Approximation Theorem 1.5 of Ch. 2) that f|M_j = g_j|M_j, where g_j is C¹". The printed arguments are copied with these errata corrections to the printed proof of 1.2:
 - in (1) read "F_j(ℝⁿ) ⊆ E_j ∪ ⋃_i G_ij(ℝⁿ)" (not "graph F_j");
 - the measure in the choice of G_ij is Lⁿ;
 - the garbled sentence reads "by the area formula Hⁿ(G_ij({x : JG_ij(x) = 0})) = 0";
 - "G_ij(B_σ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold of ℝ^{n+ℓ}" (not "of ℝⁿ").
Siblings used: c1_approx (Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5), c1_tangent (tangent plane of a C¹ disk), and im_calculus (a) (locality of approximate tangent spaces; called TL below, used with U = ℝ^P).

Notation. N := n + 1. H^N := μHE[N]; on ℝ^N it equals L^N, the Lebesgue measure. For a map ψ that is C¹ near y, Q_ψ(y) := Dψ(y)(ℝ^N). "Borel image" refers to Mathlib `MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn`: the image of a Borel set under a map that is continuous and injective on it is Borel. A map that is C¹ on an open set containing a compact convex set C is Lipschitz on C (mean value inequality). Then H^N(ψ(Z)) ≤ Lip(ψ|_C)^N·H^N(Z) for Z ⊆ C (SimonGMT `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn`).

0. Conventions. All index families below are countable; a finite or empty family is padded to one indexed by ℕ with dummy entries (ψ, V, Y, F) := (0, ∅, ∅, 0), which satisfy every required property vacuously (∅ is open, closure ∅ = ∅ is compact and contained in ∅). If P = 0, then H^N(M) = 0 (N ≥ 1 > 0 = dim ℝ⁰), and the family of dummy entries works; so assume P ≥ 1.

1. Lipschitz parametrisations (Definition 1.1, i.e. CountablyRectifiable). M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_i F_i(ℝ^N) with H^N(M₀) = 0 and each F_i : ℝ^N → ℝ^P Lipschitz.

2. C¹ approximation of the parametrisations (proof of 1.2, "only if"). Fix i and k ≥ 1. Apply c1_approx to each coordinate F_i^{(l)} := ⟨F_i, e_l⟩ (l = 1, …, P; Lipschitz) with ε = 2^{−k}/P, obtaining C¹ functions g^{(l)}. Put G_{ik} := Σ_l g^{(l)}e_l, a C¹ map ℝ^N → ℝ^P.
 - Z_{ik} := {y : F_i(y) ≠ G_{ik}(y)} ⊆ ⋃_l {F_i^{(l)} ≠ g^{(l)}}, so L^N(Z_{ik}) < 2^{−k}.
 - Z_i := ⋂_k Z_{ik} is L^N-null, and ℝ^N = Z_i ∪ ⋃_k {F_i = G_{ik}}.
 - Hence F_i(ℝ^N) ⊆ F_i(Z_i) ∪ ⋃_k G_{ik}(ℝ^N) (corrected (1)), and H^N(F_i(Z_i)) ≤ Lip(F_i)^N·H^N(Z_i) = 0.

3. Removing critical points and localising to embedded disks.
 - For each (i, k), Crit_{ik} := {y : DG_{ik}(y) is not injective} satisfies H^N(G_{ik}(Crit_{ik})) = 0 by the area formula (SimonGMT `area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero`; G_{ik} is differentiable everywhere).
 - Let y ∉ Crit_{ik}, so A := DG_{ik}(y) is injective, and put m_y := min_{|e|=1}|Ae| > 0. By continuity of DG_{ik} choose ρ_y > 0 such that ‖DG_{ik}(w) − A‖ ≤ m_y/2 for w ∈ B_y := ball(y, ρ_y). Then for w ∈ B_y, DG_{ik}(w) is injective, since |DG_{ik}(w)e| ≥ m_y/2 for unit e. For a, b ∈ B_y (a convex set), |G_{ik}(a) − G_{ik}(b) − A(a − b)| ≤ (m_y/2)|a − b|, so |G_{ik}(a) − G_{ik}(b)| ≥ (m_y/2)|a − b|; in particular G_{ik} is injective on B_y. (This is the printed "G_ij(B_σ(x)) is an embedded C¹ submanifold".)
 - ℝ^N is second countable, so countably many such balls B_y cover ℝ^N ∖ Crit_{ik}.
 Enumerate all pairs (G_{ik}, B_y) obtained as (ψ_a, V_a), a ∈ ℕ. Then M ⊆ N₁ ∪ ⋃_a ψ_a(V_a), where N₁ := M₀ ∪ ⋃_i F_i(Z_i) ∪ ⋃_{i,k} G_{ik}(Crit_{ik}) has H^N(N₁) = 0. Each ψ_a is C¹ on ℝ^N, V_a is an open ball, and ψ_a is injective on V_a with injective derivative there.

4. Closed balls. For each a, choose countably many closed balls B̄ = closedBall(q, ρ) with q ∈ ℚ^N and ρ ∈ ℚ_{>0} such that closedBall(q, 2ρ) ⊆ V_a, covering V_a. (V_a is open and each of its points lies in such a ball.)

5. C¹ approximation of f on each ball (proof of 2.4: "using the C¹ Approximation Theorem 1.5"). Fix a and B̄ = closedBall(q, ρ) from step 4.
 - ψ_a is Lipschitz on the convex compact set closedBall(q, 2ρ) ⊆ V_a, so u := f∘ψ_a is Lipschitz on B̄.
 - Let ū : ℝ^N → ℝ be a Lipschitz extension of u|_{B̄} (McShane, Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`).
 - For k ≥ 1 apply c1_approx to ū with ε = 2^{−k}: C¹ functions F_{a,B̄,k} with L^N({ū ≠ F_{a,B̄,k}}) < 2^{−k}.
 - Z_{a,B̄} := B̄ ∩ ⋂_k {ū ≠ F_{a,B̄,k}} is L^N-null, and B̄ = Z_{a,B̄} ∪ ⋃_k (B̄ ∩ {ū = F_{a,B̄,k}}).
 - Each B̄ ∩ {ū = F_{a,B̄,k}} is closed, since both functions are continuous.

6. Raw pieces. Enumerate the triples (a, B̄, k) as b ∈ ℕ. Put ψ'_b := ψ_a, V'_b := V_a, F'_b := F_{a,B̄,k}, and Y'_b := B̄ ∩ {ū = F'_b} ∩ ψ_a⁻¹(M). Y'_b is Borel: a closed set intersected with the preimage of a Borel set under a continuous map.
 - For y ∈ Y'_b: f(ψ'_b(y)) = u(y) = ū(y) = F'_b(y).
 - closure(Y'_b) ⊆ B̄ ⊆ V'_b, and B̄ is compact.
 - ψ'_b(Y'_b) ⊆ M.
 - Coverage. M ∩ ψ_a(V_a) ⊆ ⋃_{B̄} ψ_a(B̄ ∩ ψ_a⁻¹(M)) ⊆ ⋃_{B̄,k} ψ'_b(Y'_b) ∪ ⋃_{B̄} ψ_a(Z_{a,B̄}). Each ψ_a(Z_{a,B̄}) is H^N-null, being the image of an L^N-null subset of B̄ under a map Lipschitz on B̄. With step 3, H^N(M ∖ ⋃_b ψ'_b(Y'_b)) = 0.

7. Disjointification (Remark 1.3). A_b := ψ'_b(Y'_b) is Borel (Borel image; ψ'_b is continuous and injective on Y'_b ⊆ V'_b). Put D_b := A_b ∖ ⋃_{b'<b} A_{b'} (Borel) and Y''_b := Y'_b ∩ ψ'_b⁻¹(D_b), which is Borel. Since ψ(S ∩ ψ⁻¹(T)) = ψ(S) ∩ T and D_b ⊆ A_b = ψ'_b(Y'_b), ψ'_b(Y''_b) = D_b. The D_b are pairwise disjoint, and ⋃_b D_b = ⋃_b A_b.

8. Tangent planes (Remark 1.5(2), proof of 1.6 "⇒"). Fix b, coming from (a, B̄ = closedBall(q, ρ), k).
 - S_b := ψ'_b(closedBall(q, 2ρ)) is compact, hence Borel, and H^N(S_b) < ∞ (Lipschitz image of a ball).
 - By c1_tangent (g := ψ'_b, U := V'_b, closed ball closedBall(q, 2ρ) ⊆ V'_b, on which ψ'_b is injective with injective derivative): for every y ∈ ball(q, 2ρ) ⊇ B̄ ⊇ Y''_b, S_b has approximate tangent space Q_{ψ'_b}(y) at ψ'_b(y).
 - TL (im_calculus (a), U = ℝ^P, dimension N) for the Borel pair D_b ⊆ S_b (S_b has finite H^N-measure): for H^N-a.e. x ∈ D_b and every subspace Q, D_b has approximate tangent space Q at x iff S_b does.
 - TL for the Borel pair D_b ⊆ M (M is locally H^N-finite by hypothesis): for H^N-a.e. x ∈ D_b and every Q, D_b has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M does.
 - Hence for H^N-a.e. x = ψ'_b(y) ∈ D_b (y ∈ Y''_b), M has approximate tangent space Q_{ψ'_b}(y) at x. Let E_b ⊆ D_b be the H^N-null exceptional set, and E'_b ⊇ E_b a Borel H^N-null set (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.exists_measurable_superset_of_null`).
 - Put Y_b := Y''_b ∖ ψ'_b⁻¹(E'_b), which is Borel. For y ∈ Y_b, ψ'_b(y) ∉ E_b, so M has approximate tangent space Dψ'_b(y)(ℝ^N) at ψ'_b(y).

9. Conclusion. Put ψ_j := ψ'_j, V_j := V'_j, F_j := F'_j, and Y_j as in step 8. Then:
 - ψ_j is C¹ on ℝ^N, V_j is open, and ψ_j is injective on V_j with injective derivative there (step 3).
 - F_j is C¹.
 - Y_j is Borel, and closure(Y_j) ⊆ B̄ ⊆ V_j with B̄ compact, so closure(Y_j) is compact (closed subset of a compact set).
 - ψ_j(Y_j) ⊆ D_j ⊆ M.
 - f(ψ_j(y)) = F_j(y) for y ∈ Y_j (step 6).
 - For y ∈ Y_j, M has approximate tangent space Dψ_j(y)(ℝ^N) at ψ_j(y) (step 8).
 - The sets ψ_j(Y_j) ⊆ D_j are pairwise disjoint (step 7).
 - M ∖ ⋃_j ψ_j(Y_j) ⊆ (M ∖ ⋃_b A_b) ∪ ⋃_b E'_b, so H^N(M ∖ ⋃_j ψ_j(Y_j)) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Approximate each Lipschitz parametrisation F_i coordinatewise by C¹ maps G_ik agreeing with F_i off L^N-small sets (c1_approx); F_i(ℝ^N) ⊆ null ∪ ⋃_k G_ik(ℝ^N).
Discard the H^N-null critical images G_ik({DG_ik not injective}) (area formula) and cover the rest by countably many balls on which G_ik is an injective immersion.
On closed balls B̄ with closedBall(q,2ρ) ⊆ V_a, approximate a Lipschitz extension of f∘ψ_a by C¹ functions (c1_approx) to get pieces Y'_b with f∘ψ = F on Y'_b, covering M up to a null set.
Disjointify the images (Remark 1.3).
Tangent planes: c1_tangent for ψ(closedBall(q,2ρ)) and TL (im_calculus (a)) for D_b ⊆ S_b and D_b ⊆ M give T_{ψ(y)}M = Dψ(y)(ℝ^N) a.e.; remove the null exceptional set.

subproblems.title: Co-area formula and level-set structure on one C¹ chart (Simon Ch. 2, 6.3, 6.4 and 6.6 for the submanifold ψ(V))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let ψ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P be C¹, V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} open with ψ injective on V and Dψ(y) injective for y ∈ V, F : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ C¹, and Y ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} Borel with closure(Y) compact and contained in V. Let G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P satisfy, for every y ∈ Y, G(ψ(y)) ∈ Dψ(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) and ⟨G(ψ(y)), Dψ(y)e⟩ = DF(y)e for all e ∈ ℝ^{n+1} (so G∘ψ is the gradient of F∘ψ⁻¹ along ψ(V)). Write Hᵏ = μHE[k]. Then: (i) for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], the function t ↦ ∫_{ψ(Y ∩ F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{ψ(Y ∩ F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_{ψ(Y)} |G| g dH^{n+1}; (ii) for L¹-a.e. t, the set S_t := ψ(Y ∩ F⁻¹(t)) is countably n-rectifiable, and for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S_t we have G(x) ≠ 0 and, for the y ∈ Y with ψ(y) = x, S_t has approximate tangent space Dψ(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) ∩ G(x)^⊥ at x.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, §6: the co-area formula 6.3 for C¹ maps on C¹ submanifolds, its weighted form 6.6, and the Sard-type Theorem 6.4 (chapter-02.txt lines 1405–1530, printed pp. 65–67), here for the submanifold ψ(V) and the real-valued C¹ function F∘ψ⁻¹. Simon prints no proof of 6.3; he says it "uses an approximation argument based on the linear case 6.2" and refers to [Fed69] (Federer 3.2.11–3.2.12). For a real-valued C¹ function with nonvanishing gradient, the implicit function theorem reduces it to Fubini's theorem and the area formula. That standard argument is written out below. The critical set is treated with Eilenberg's inequality (sibling eilenberg), as in Federer 3.2.12. The level-set structure is Simon's 6.4 (f⁻¹(y) ∖ C is a C¹ submanifold) together with the proof of Ch. 3, 1.6 "⇒" (sibling c1_tangent and locality im_calculus (a), called TL).

Notation. N := n + 1; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; on ℝᵏ it equals Lebesgue measure Lᵏ. For y ∈ V let A_y := Dψ(y) (injective), J(y) := J(A_y) = √det(A_y*A_y) > 0, and Q(y) := A_y(ℝ^N). ∇F(y) is the gradient of F. Ȳ := closure(Y), compact ⊆ V. For a linear map B from a k-dimensional space, J(B) := √det(B*B).

0. Preliminaries on the chart.
 (a) Bi-Lipschitz. There are 0 < m ≤ Λ with m|a − b| ≤ |ψ(a) − ψ(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b| for a, b ∈ Ȳ.
  - Upper bound. Ȳ is compact, so Ȳ ⊆ closedBall(0, R₀) for some R₀. ψ is C¹ on all of ℝ^N, so Λ := sup_{closedBall(0,R₀)} ‖Dψ‖ < ∞, and the mean value inequality on this convex ball gives the bound.
  - Lower bound, by contradiction. Suppose there are a_k ≠ b_k in Ȳ with |ψ(a_k) − ψ(b_k)| < k⁻¹|a_k − b_k|. By compactness pass to a subsequence with a_k → a ∈ Ȳ, b_k → b ∈ Ȳ and e_k := (a_k − b_k)/|a_k − b_k| → e, |e| = 1.
   If a ≠ b, continuity gives ψ(a) = ψ(b), contradicting injectivity of ψ on V ⊇ Ȳ.
   If a = b, choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(a, ρ) ⊆ V. For large k, a_k, b_k ∈ closedBall(a, ρ) (convex), and ψ(a_k) − ψ(b_k) = ∫₀¹ Dψ(b_k + τ(a_k − b_k))(a_k − b_k) dτ. Dividing by |a_k − b_k| and using continuity of Dψ at a gives |Dψ(a)e| = lim_k |ψ(a_k) − ψ(b_k)|/|a_k − b_k| = 0, contradicting injectivity of Dψ(a).
  Hence ψ|_Ȳ is injective and continuous on a compact set, so it is a homeomorphism onto ψ(Ȳ) with continuous inverse. ψ maps Borel subsets of Y onto Borel sets (Mathlib `MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn`).
 (b) The vector G(ψ(y)). For y ∈ V put Ĝ(y) := A_y(A_y*A_y)⁻¹∇F(y); Ĝ is continuous on V, and Ĝ(y) is the unique vector of Q(y) with ⟨Ĝ(y), A_ye⟩ = DF(y)e for all e. (Writing a vector of Q(y) as A_y w, the condition ⟨A_y w, A_y e⟩ = ⟨∇F(y), e⟩ for all e says A_y*A_y w = ∇F(y).) So the hypotheses give G(ψ(y)) = Ĝ(y) for y ∈ Y. Consequences:
  - Ĝ(y) = 0 iff ∇F(y) = 0;
  - Γ := sup_{y∈Ȳ}|Ĝ(y)| < ∞ (continuity on the compact Ȳ), so |G| ≤ Γ on ψ(Y);
  - on ψ(Y), G = Ĝ∘(ψ|_Ȳ)⁻¹, which is Borel on ψ(Y) (continuous inverse chart of (a)).
 (c) Jacobian identity in the target. Let y ∈ V with ∇F(y) ≠ 0, K_y := ker DF(y) (dimension n), ν := ∇F(y)/|∇F(y)|, and J_K(y) := J(A_y|_{K_y}) (computed with an orthonormal basis of K_y). Then
  A_y(K_y) = Q(y) ∩ Ĝ(y)^⊥ and J_K(y)·|∇F(y)| = |Ĝ(y)|·J(y).
  Proof. Take an orthonormal basis (k_1, …, k_n) of K_y, so (ν, k_1, …, k_n) is orthonormal in ℝ^N. The N-volume of (A_yν, A_yk_1, …, A_yk_n) is J(y), and it equals J_K(y)·dist(A_yν, A_y(K_y)) (base times height). Put Ĝ := Ĝ(y); Ĝ ∈ Q(y), and ⟨Ĝ, A_yk⟩ = DF(y)k = 0 for k ∈ K_y, so Ĝ ⊥ A_y(K_y). Also ⟨Ĝ, A_yν⟩ = DF(y)ν = |∇F(y)| ≠ 0, so Ĝ ≠ 0. Since A_y(K_y) is n-dimensional in the (n+1)-dimensional Q(y), Q(y) ∩ Ĝ^⊥ = A_y(K_y), and dist(A_yν, A_y(K_y)) = |⟨A_yν, Ĝ⟩|/|Ĝ| = |∇F(y)|/|Ĝ|. Hence J(y) = J_K(y)|∇F(y)|/|Ĝ|. For y ∈ Y, Ĝ(y) = G(ψ(y)).

1. The critical part (Sard-type Theorem 6.4). Let Y_c := Y ∩ {∇F = 0}, a Borel set. On ψ(Y_c), G = Ĝ∘(ψ|_Ȳ)⁻¹ = 0 by 0(b). We show Hⁿ(Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t)) = 0 for L¹-a.e. t.
 - Let Ȳ₁ := {w : dist(w, Ȳ) ≤ 1} (compact) and c₁ := L^N(Ȳ₁) < ∞. Let ε ∈ (0, 1]. By uniform continuity of DF on Ȳ₁ choose δ ∈ (0, 1] with ‖DF(w) − DF(w')‖ ≤ ε for w, w' ∈ Ȳ₁ with |w − w'| ≤ δ.
 - Take the half-open dyadic cubes of side s with s√N ≤ δ that meet Y_c, say (Q_l)_l. They are disjoint. Each lies within distance δ ≤ 1 of a point p_l ∈ Y_c, so Q_l ⊆ Ȳ₁ and ‖DF‖ ≤ ε on Q_l (as DF(p_l) = 0). Hence Σ_l L^N(Q_l) ≤ c₁, and F is ε-Lipschitz on each convex Q_l (mean value inequality).
 - By eilenberg (in ℝ^N, with A := Q_l ∩ Y_c and Lipschitz constant ε) there are Borel φ_l with Hⁿ(Q_l ∩ Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t)) ≤ φ_l(t) and ∫φ_l ≤ C·ε·H^N(Q_l) = C·ε·L^N(Q_l).
 - Φ_ε := Σ_l φ_l is Borel, Hⁿ(Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t)) ≤ Φ_ε(t) for every t (countable subadditivity), and ∫Φ_ε ≤ C·ε·c₁.
 - Put Φ := liminf_k Φ_{2^{−k}}. Then Hⁿ(Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t)) ≤ Φ(t) for all t, and by Fatou ∫Φ ≤ liminf_k C2^{−k}c₁ = 0. So Φ = 0 a.e.
 Consequently, by 0(a), Hⁿ(ψ(Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t))) ≤ Λⁿ·Hⁿ(Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t)) = 0 for a.e. t (SimonGMT `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn`).

2. Local straightening of F on the regular part.
 - Y_r := Y ∩ {∇F ≠ 0} is Borel. For y₀ ∈ V with ∇F(y₀) ≠ 0, let (u_1, …, u_n) be an orthonormal basis of ∇F(y₀)^⊥ and define the C¹ self-map Φ_{y₀} : ℝ^N → ℝ^N by Φ_{y₀}(y)_0 := F(y) and Φ_{y₀}(y)_i := ⟨u_i, y⟩ (i = 1, …, n), using the coordinates indexed by Fin (n+1) = {0, …, n}. We write Φ_{y₀}(y) = (F(y), π_{y₀}(y)) with π_{y₀}(y) := (⟨u_i, y⟩)_{i=1..n} ∈ ℝⁿ.
 - DΦ_{y₀}(y₀) is invertible: its kernel is ∇F(y₀)^⊥ ∩ (span u)^⊥ = 0. By the inverse function theorem (Mathlib `ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph`, in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.ContDiff, to be added to the imports; C¹ of the inverse by `OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm`) there is an open W_{y₀} ∋ y₀ with W_{y₀} ⊆ V ∩ {∇F ≠ 0} such that Φ_{y₀}|_{W_{y₀}} is a C¹ diffeomorphism onto an open set Ω_{y₀} ⊆ ℝ^N, with det DΦ_{y₀} ≠ 0 on W_{y₀}.
 - By second countability choose y_1, y_2, … with Y_r ⊆ ⋃_k W_k (W_k := W_{y_k}, Φ_k := Φ_{y_k}, Ω_k := Ω_{y_k}). Put Y_k := (Y_r ∩ W_k) ∖ ⋃_{k'<k} W_{k'}: Borel, pairwise disjoint, with union Y_r.
 - Splitting off the coordinate 0, ℝ^N = ℝ^{1+n} ≅ ℝ × ℝⁿ, (s, w) ↔ (s, w_1, …, w_n). Under this identification Lebesgue measure on ℝ^N is the product measure L¹ ⊗ Lⁿ (Mathlib `EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp` and `MeasureTheory.measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove` at index 0). For t ∈ ℝ put Ω_k^t := {w ∈ ℝⁿ : (t, w) ∈ Ω_k} (open) and χ_k^t(w) := ψ(Φ_k⁻¹(t, w)) for w ∈ Ω_k^t, where Φ_k⁻¹ is the inverse of Φ_k|_{W_k}.
 - χ_k^t is C¹ on Ω_k^t and injective (Φ_k⁻¹ is injective and ψ is injective on V). Let y := Φ_k⁻¹(t, w) and B := DΦ_k(y). Then Dχ_k^t(w) = A_y∘B⁻¹∘ι, where ι(w') := (0, w'). B⁻¹∘ι maps ℝⁿ isomorphically onto K_y, because DF(y)B⁻¹(0, w') = 0. Hence Dχ_k^t(w) is injective, with image A_y(K_y) = Q(y) ∩ Ĝ(y)^⊥ (0(c)); for y ∈ Y this is Q(y) ∩ G(ψ(y))^⊥.
 - Jacobian identity in the domain: J(B⁻¹∘ι)·|det B| = |∇F(y)|. Indeed |det B⁻¹| is the N-volume of (B⁻¹(1, 0), B⁻¹ι e_1, …, B⁻¹ι e_n), which is J(B⁻¹ι)·dist(B⁻¹(1, 0), K_y), and DF(y)B⁻¹(1, 0) = 1 gives dist(B⁻¹(1, 0), K_y) = 1/|∇F(y)|.
 - Since J(A_y∘B⁻¹∘ι) = J_K(y)·J(B⁻¹ι) (B⁻¹ι maps onto K_y), 0(c) gives for every y = Φ_k⁻¹(t, w) ∈ W_k:
  (★) J(Dχ_k^t(w))·|det DΦ_k(y)| = J_K(y)·|∇F(y)| = |Ĝ(y)|·J(y).

3. The formula on one piece Y_k. Fix k and a Borel g ≥ 0 on ℝ^P. Put h_k := [|Ĝ|·(g∘ψ)·J/|det DΦ_k|]∘Φ_k⁻¹ on Ω_k (and 0 off Ω_k). It is Borel, since Ĝ, J, DΦ_k and Φ_k⁻¹ are continuous on the relevant open sets and g is Borel.
 (a) Right side. Weighted injective area formula for ψ on Y_k (SimonGMT `weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative`; ψ is differentiable with injective derivative on Y_k ⊆ V and injective there), and G(ψ(y)) = Ĝ(y) on Y:
  ∫_{ψ(Y_k)} |G| g dH^N = ∫_{Y_k} |Ĝ(y)| g(ψ(y)) J(y) dy.
  By change of variables y = Φ_k⁻¹(t, w) (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul` for the self-map Φ_k of ℝ^N on Y_k ⊆ W_k) and Tonelli in the product coordinates, this equals
  ∫_{Φ_k(Y_k)} h_k = ∫_ℝ ∫_{Ω_k^t} 1_{Φ_k(Y_k)}(t, w)·h_k(t, w) dw dt.
 (b) Left side for a fixed t. Since F(Φ_k⁻¹(t, w)) = t, ψ(Y_k ∩ F⁻¹(t)) = χ_k^t({w ∈ Ω_k^t : (t, w) ∈ Φ_k(Y_k)}). The weighted area formula for the injective C¹ map χ_k^t with injective derivative (from ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ there) gives
  ∫_{ψ(Y_k∩F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ = ∫_{Ω_k^t} 1_{Φ_k(Y_k)}(t, w)·g(χ_k^t(w))·J(Dχ_k^t(w)) dw.
  By (★), g(χ_k^t(w))J(Dχ_k^t(w)) = h_k(t, w) whenever (t, w) ∈ Φ_k(Y_k) ⊆ Ω_k.
 (c) So for every t, ∫_{ψ(Y_k∩F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ = ∫ 1_{Φ_k(Y_k)}(t, w)h_k(t, w) dw. By Tonelli this is a measurable function of t, and integrating over t and using (a):
  ∫_ℝ ∫_{ψ(Y_k ∩ F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_{ψ(Y_k)} |G| g dH^N.

4. Proof of (i). The Borel sets ψ(Y_k) (k ∈ ℕ) and ψ(Y_c) are pairwise disjoint (ψ is injective on Y) and cover ψ(Y). For every t, ψ(Y ∩ F⁻¹(t)) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets ψ(Y_k ∩ F⁻¹(t)) and ψ(Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t)). By countable additivity of set integrals, ∫_{ψ(Y∩F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ = Σ_k ∫_{ψ(Y_k∩F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ + ∫_{ψ(Y_c∩F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ. The last term vanishes for a.e. t by step 1, and the sum is a measurable function of t (step 3). Hence t ↦ ∫_{ψ(Y∩F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable. By monotone convergence and step 3,
 ∫_ℝ ∫_{ψ(Y∩F⁻¹(t))} g dHⁿ dt = Σ_k ∫_{ψ(Y_k)} |G| g dH^N = ∫_{ψ(Y)} |G| g dH^N,
 using G = 0 on ψ(Y_c).

5. Good levels. Apply (i) with g ≡ 1: ∫_ℝ Hⁿ(S_t) dt = ∫_{ψ(Y)} |G| dH^N ≤ Γ·H^N(ψ(Ȳ)) ≤ Γ·Λ^N·L^N(Ȳ) < ∞ (0(a), 0(b)). Let T₀ be the set of t with Hⁿ(S_t) < ∞ and Hⁿ(ψ(Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t))) = 0. By this and step 1, T₀ has full L¹-measure.

6. Rectifiability. Fix t ∈ T₀. S_t ∖ ψ(Y_c ∩ F⁻¹(t)) ⊆ ⋃_k χ_k^t(Ω_k^t). Cover each open Ω_k^t by countably many closed balls B̄ ⊆ Ω_k^t. On each B̄, χ_k^t is Lipschitz (it is C¹ on the open Ω_k^t ⊇ B̄, so the mean value inequality on the convex compact B̄ applies), so it extends to a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (McShane in each coordinate) whose range contains χ_k^t(B̄). Thus S_t is contained in an Hⁿ-null set together with countably many Lipschitz images of ℝⁿ, i.e. S_t is countably n-rectifiable.

7. Tangent planes. Fix t ∈ T₀. S_t is Borel (0(a)) and Hⁿ(S_t) < ∞.
 - Fix k and a closed ball closedBall(w₀, 2ρ) ⊆ Ω_k^t (countably many with rational data suffice to cover Ω_k^t by the balls closedBall(w₀, ρ)). Let Σ := χ_k^t(closedBall(w₀, 2ρ)): compact, Hⁿ(Σ) < ∞.
 - By c1_tangent (d := n, g := χ_k^t, U := Ω_k^t; χ_k^t is injective on the closed ball with injective derivative), for every w ∈ ball(w₀, 2ρ), Σ has approximate tangent space Dχ_k^t(w)(ℝⁿ) at χ_k^t(w). By step 2 this space is Q(y) ∩ Ĝ(y)^⊥, where y = Φ_k⁻¹(t, w); for y ∈ Y it is Q(y) ∩ G(ψ(y))^⊥.
 - Let A := S_t ∩ ψ(Y_k) ∩ χ_k^t(closedBall(w₀, ρ)), a Borel subset of Σ.
 - TL (im_calculus (a), U = ℝ^P, dimension n) for A ⊆ Σ and for A ⊆ S_t (both locally Hⁿ-finite): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A, S_t has the same approximate tangent spaces at x as Σ, namely Q(y) ∩ G(x)^⊥ for the y ∈ Y_k with ψ(y) = x.
 - These countably many sets A cover S_t ∩ ψ(Y_r) (every w ∈ Ω_k^t lies in some closedBall(w₀, ρ) of the family), and G ≠ 0 on ψ(Y_r) (0(b)). The rest of S_t is S_t ∩ ψ(Y_c), which is Hⁿ-null since t ∈ T₀.
 Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S_t: G(x) ≠ 0, and for the unique y ∈ Y with ψ(y) = x (ψ is injective on V), S_t has approximate tangent space Dψ(y)(ℝ^N) ∩ (span G(x))^⊥ at x. This is (ii). ∎
proof_key_steps: On Ȳ the chart ψ is bi-Lipschitz, G(ψ y) = Dψ(Dψ*Dψ)⁻¹∇F(y), and J_K·|∇F| = |G|·J with Dψ(ker DF) = range Dψ ∩ G^⊥ (linear algebra).
Critical part: Hⁿ({∇F=0} ∩ Y ∩ F⁻¹(t)) = 0 for a.e. t, by Eilenberg on small cubes where F is ε-Lipschitz (Sard-type 6.4).

Regular part: straighten F by the inverse function theorem, Φ = (F, π); change of variables, Tonelli and the area formula for the level parametrisations χ^t = ψ∘Φ⁻¹(t,·), with the identity J(Dχ^t)|det DΦ| = |G∘ψ| J, give the co-area formula on each piece.
Sum over pieces for (i); local finiteness of the slices for a.e. t; rectifiability from the Lipschitz parametrisations χ^t.
Tangent planes of the slices: c1_tangent for χ^t(closed balls) and TL (im_calculus (a)) give T_xS_t = Dψ(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) ∩ G(x)^⊥ with G(x) ≠ 0, a.e.

subproblems.title: Co-area formula, tangential gradient and slices of a countably rectifiable set (Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1; Ch. 3, 2.1, 2.8–2.10)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably (n+1)-rectifiable with H^{n+1}(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K (Hᵏ = μHE[k]), and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz. Then there is a Borel map G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (Simon's ∇^M f) with |G(x)| ≤ L for every x such that: (1) (tangential gradient) for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ M, M has an approximate tangent space at x, namely T_xM := approxTangentPlane (n+1) M x, G(x) ∈ T_xM, and for every ε > 0, r^{−(n+1)}·H^{n+1}({y ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : |f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩| > ε|y − x|}) → 0 as r ↓ 0; (2) (co-area) for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |G| g dH^{n+1}; (3) (slices) for L¹-a.e. t, M ∩ f⁻¹(t) is countably n-rectifiable, and for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹(t): G(x) ≠ 0 and M ∩ f⁻¹(t) has approximate tangent space T_xM ∩ G(x)^⊥ at x.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1 and its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 1156–1195, printed p. 154): "(1) is just a restatement of 2.10(2) of Ch. 3, and (2) follows from 1.6 of Ch. 3 together with the facts that … ∇^M f(x) ∈ T_xM … and ⟨∇^M f(x), τ⟩ = 0 ∀ τ ∈ T_xM_t … The last part of the lemma is just a restatement of the appropriate version of the co-area formula". The cited Ch. 3 results are 2.1 (∇^M f(y) := ∇^{N_j} f(y) on M_j ⊆ N_j), 2.8–2.9 ("this follows from the C¹ case (§6 of Ch. 2) by using the decomposition M = ⋃ M_j of Remark 1.3 and the C¹ Approximation Theorem 1.5 of Ch. 2") and 2.10(2) (chapter-03.txt lines 327–445). These printed arguments are followed:
 - the decomposition into C¹ pieces with C¹ representatives of f is the sibling chart_pieces;
 - the C¹ case on one piece is the sibling chart_coarea;
 - the null part of the decomposition is handled by Eilenberg's inequality (sibling eilenberg; Simon uses the "easily checked fact" that null sets have null images in the proof of 2.4);
 - locality of approximate tangent spaces is im_calculus (a) (called TL; used with U = ℝ^P).
Here M_t is all of M ∩ f⁻¹(t), not Simon's M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t); by (2) the two differ by an Hⁿ-null set for a.e. t. The tangential gradient is characterised in (1) by approximate differentiability along M. This is the form in which the siblings lipschitz_leibniz and slice_family use it.

Notation. N := n + 1, Hᵏ := μHE[k]. B_r(x) := ball(x, r). For a set S and a point x, η_{x,r}(S) := r⁻¹(S − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap).

1. Pieces. Apply chart_pieces to (M, f), obtaining ψ_j, V_j, Y_j, F_j (j ∈ ℕ). Put A_j := ψ_j(Y_j) (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⊆ M) and M₀ := M ∖ ⋃_j A_j (Borel, H^N(M₀) = 0).
 - For y ∈ Y_j write B_{j,y} := Dψ_j(y) and Q_j(y) := B_{j,y}(ℝ^N). M has approximate tangent space Q_j(y) at ψ_j(y). By uniqueness (SimonGMT `HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`), approxTangentPlane N M (ψ_j(y)) = Q_j(y), and M has approximate tangent space approxTangentPlane N M x at every x ∈ ⋃_j A_j.
 - Bi-Lipschitz charts. Let Ȳ_j := closure(Y_j), compact ⊆ V_j. There are 0 < m_j ≤ Λ_j with m_j|a − b| ≤ |ψ_j(a) − ψ_j(b)| ≤ Λ_j|a − b| for a, b ∈ Ȳ_j.
  Upper bound: Ȳ_j lies in a closed ball, on which ‖Dψ_j‖ is bounded (ψ_j is C¹ on ℝ^N); apply the mean value inequality.
  Lower bound, by contradiction: if a_k ≠ b_k in Ȳ_j with |ψ_j(a_k) − ψ_j(b_k)| < k⁻¹|a_k − b_k|, pass to a subsequence with a_k → a, b_k → b and (a_k − b_k)/|a_k − b_k| → e, |e| = 1. If a ≠ b, then ψ_j(a) = ψ_j(b), contradicting injectivity on V_j. If a = b, write ψ_j(a_k) − ψ_j(b_k) = ∫₀¹ Dψ_j(b_k + τ(a_k − b_k))(a_k − b_k) dτ on a closed ball around a inside V_j and let k → ∞ to get Dψ_j(a)e = 0, contradicting injectivity of Dψ_j(a).
  Hence ψ_j|_{Ȳ_j} is a homeomorphism onto its image, with continuous inverse.

2. Definition of G (Simon's 2.1). For x = ψ_j(y) ∈ A_j put g_j(x) := B_{j,y}(B_{j,y}*B_{j,y})⁻¹∇F_j(y). This is the unique vector of Q_j(y) with ⟨g_j(x), B_{j,y}e⟩ = DF_j(y)e for all e ∈ ℝ^N, and g_j is Borel on A_j (continuous in y, composed with the continuous inverse chart).
 (a) |g_j| ≤ L at H^N-a.e. point of A_j.
  - Let y ∈ Y_j be a Lebesgue density point of Y_j; L^N-a.e. point of Y_j is one (Mathlib `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div`). Let e be a unit vector.
  - There are y_k ∈ Y_j with y_k → y and (y_k − y)/|y_k − y| → e. Otherwise, for some δ ∈ (0, 1), the truncated cone C_δ := {y' : 0 < |y' − y| < δ, ⟨y' − y, e⟩ > (1 − δ)|y' − y|} does not meet Y_j. C_δ ∩ B_r(y) occupies a fixed fraction c_δ > 0 of L^N(B_r(y)) for every r < δ (scaling), so L^N(Y_j ∩ B_r(y)) ≤ (1 − c_δ)L^N(B_r(y)), contradicting density 1 at y.
  - Since F_j = f∘ψ_j on Y_j, |F_j(y_k) − F_j(y)| ≤ L|ψ_j(y_k) − ψ_j(y)|. Dividing by |y_k − y| and letting k → ∞ gives |DF_j(y)e| ≤ L|B_{j,y}e|. Hence |⟨g_j(x), v⟩| ≤ L|v| for v ∈ Q_j(y), and v = g_j(x) gives |g_j(x)| ≤ L.
  - The non-density points form an L^N-null subset of Y_j, whose ψ_j-image is H^N-null (ψ_j is Lipschitz on Y_j).
  So the Borel set {y ∈ Y_j : |g_j(ψ_j(y))| > L} is L^N-null. Remove it from Y_j; its image goes into M₀, which remains H^N-null. Keep the names A_j, Y_j; all properties of step 1 persist.
 (b) Put G(x) := g_j(x) for x ∈ A_j and G(x) := 0 for x ∉ ⋃_j A_j. Then G is Borel and |G| ≤ L everywhere. For every j and y ∈ Y_j: G(ψ_j(y)) ∈ Q_j(y) and ⟨G(ψ_j(y)), B_{j,y}e⟩ = DF_j(y)e for all e. These are the hypotheses of chart_coarea for (ψ_j, V_j, Y_j, F_j, G). Also G(x) ∈ Q_j(y) = approxTangentPlane N M x.

3. Conclusion (1). Fix j.
 (a) Density of M ∖ A_j. By TL for the Borel pair A_j ⊆ M (M locally H^N-finite), for H^N-a.e. x ∈ A_j the sets A_j and M have the same approximate tangent spaces at x. So A_j has approximate tangent space T := approxTangentPlane N M x at x. Take φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 and φ = 1 on closedBall(0, 1). Since η_{x,r} maps B_r(x) into closedBall(0, 1) and multiplies H^N by r^{−N}, and η_{x,r}(M) is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(A_j) and η_{x,r}(M ∖ A_j):
  r^{−N}H^N((M ∖ A_j) ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} φ dH^N − ∫_{η_{x,r}(A_j)} φ dH^N → ∫_T φ − ∫_T φ = 0 as r ↓ 0.
 (b) First-order expansion along A_j. Let x = ψ_j(y), y ∈ Y_j, and ε > 0. For y' ∈ Y_j,
  f(ψ_j(y')) − f(x) = F_j(y') − F_j(y) = DF_j(y)(y' − y) + o(|y' − y|), and
  ⟨G(x), ψ_j(y') − x⟩ = ⟨G(x), B_{j,y}(y' − y)⟩ + o(|y' − y|) = DF_j(y)(y' − y) + o(|y' − y|),
  by differentiability of F_j and ψ_j at y and step 2(b). Since |y' − y| ≤ m_j⁻¹|ψ_j(y') − x|, and y' → y when ψ_j(y') → x (continuity of the inverse chart), there is r₀ > 0 with |f(x') − f(x) − ⟨G(x), x' − x⟩| ≤ ε|x' − x| for all x' ∈ A_j ∩ B_{r₀}(x).
 (c) Hence for r < r₀ the exceptional set {x' ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : |f(x') − f(x) − ⟨G(x), x' − x⟩| > ε|x' − x|} is contained in (M ∖ A_j) ∩ B_r(x), whose H^N-measure is o(r^N) by (a). With step 1 (T_xM exists and equals Q_j(y)) and step 2(b) (G(x) ∈ T_xM), (1) holds at H^N-a.e. x ∈ A_j. Since H^N(M₀) = 0, (1) holds at H^N-a.e. x ∈ M.

4. Conclusion (2) (Ch. 3, 2.8–2.9). Let g ≥ 0 be Borel.
 - For each j, f∘ψ_j = F_j on Y_j, so A_j ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ψ_j(Y_j ∩ F_j⁻¹(t)). By chart_coarea (i), t ↦ ∫_{A_j∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{A_j∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_{A_j} |G| g dH^N.
 - eilenberg with A := M₀ (H^N(M₀) = 0) gives a Borel φ ≥ Hⁿ(M₀ ∩ f⁻¹(·)) with ∫φ ≤ C·L·0 = 0. So Hⁿ(M₀ ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = 0 for a.e. t.
 - For such t, M ∩ f⁻¹(t) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets A_j ∩ f⁻¹(t) and the Hⁿ-null set M₀ ∩ f⁻¹(t). By countable additivity, ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ = Σ_j ∫_{A_j∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ.
 - So t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ is a.e. equal to a countable sum of a.e.-measurable functions, hence a.e.-measurable. By monotone convergence, ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ dt = Σ_j ∫_{A_j} |G| g dH^N = ∫_M |G| g dH^N, the last step because H^N(M₀) = 0.

5. Conclusion (3) (Lemma 4.1 (1), (2); Ch. 3, 2.10(2)). For each j, by chart_coarea (ii), for a.e. t the set S_{j,t} := A_j ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ψ_j(Y_j ∩ F_j⁻¹(t)) is countably n-rectifiable, and for Hⁿ-a.e. x = ψ_j(y) ∈ S_{j,t}: G(x) ≠ 0 and S_{j,t} has approximate tangent space Q_j(y) ∩ G(x)^⊥ at x.
 - By (2) with g := 1_{closedBall(0,k)}: ∫_ℝ Hⁿ(M ∩ f⁻¹(t) ∩ closedBall(0, k)) dt ≤ L·H^N(M ∩ closedBall(0, k)) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ. So for a.e. t, M ∩ f⁻¹(t) is locally Hⁿ-finite.
 - Let t lie in the intersection of the countably many full-measure sets above and of {t : Hⁿ(M₀ ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = 0} (step 4).
 - Rectifiability. M ∩ f⁻¹(t) ⊆ (M₀ ∩ f⁻¹(t)) ∪ ⋃_j S_{j,t}, so it is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero`, `countablyRectifiable_iUnion`, `CountablyRectifiable.mono`).
 - Tangent planes. For each j, TL (dimension n) for the Borel pair S_{j,t} ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹(t) (the latter Borel and locally Hⁿ-finite): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S_{j,t}, M ∩ f⁻¹(t) and S_{j,t} have the same approximate tangent spaces at x. With the above and Q_j(y) = approxTangentPlane N M x (step 1): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S_{j,t}, G(x) ≠ 0 and M ∩ f⁻¹(t) has approximate tangent space approxTangentPlane N M x ⊓ (span G(x))^⊥ at x.
 - Since M ∩ f⁻¹(t) = (M₀ ∩ f⁻¹(t)) ∪ ⋃_j S_{j,t} with the first set Hⁿ-null, this holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹(t). ∎
proof_key_steps: chart_pieces: M = M₀ ∪ ⨆_j ψ_j(Y_j), H^{n+1}(M₀) = 0, f∘ψ_j = F_j C¹ on Y_j, T_{ψ_j y}M = Dψ_j(y)(ℝ^{n+1}).
Define G = ∇^M f piecewise by G(ψ_j y) = Dψ_j(Dψ_j*Dψ_j)⁻¹∇F_j(y) (Simon 2.1); |G| ≤ L at density points (remove a null set); G Borel.
Approximate differentiability (1): TL makes M∖A_j of density zero at a.e. point of A_j, and f is C¹ along the chart.
Co-area (2): sum chart_coarea (i) over the pieces; the null part contributes nothing by eilenberg.
Slices (3): chart_coarea (ii) on each piece, local finiteness from (2), and TL to pass from S_{j,t} to M ∩ f⁻¹(t).

subproblems.title: Leibniz rule with a Lipschitz multiplier for an integer multiplicity current with integer multiplicity boundary (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.5(2), steps (1)–(3))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ. Let T ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) be represented by the integer multiplicity triple R_T = (M, θ, ξ) (IMRep univ (m+2)) and ∂T by R_∂ = (M', θ', ξ') (IMRep univ (m+1)). Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be K-Lipschitz (K ≥ 0) and H : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel with |H(x)| ≤ K for all x, such that H is an approximate tangential gradient of h along M: for H^{m+2}-a.e. x ∈ M, M has approximate tangent space T_xM := approxTangentPlane (m+2) M x at x, H(x) ∈ T_xM, and for every ε > 0, r^{−(m+2)}·H^{m+2}({y ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : |h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩| > ε|y − x|}) → 0 as r ↓ 0 (Hᵏ = μHE[k]). Then for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P): ∫_{M'} θ' h ⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{m+1} − ∫_M θ h ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{m+2} = ∫_M θ ⟨H♭ ∧ ω, ξ⟩ dH^{m+2}, where H♭ = ⟨H, ·⟩ (innerSL ℝ H) and H♭ ∧ ω := alternatizeUncurryFin(H♭.smulRight ω), i.e. (β∧ω)(v₀,…,v_{m+1}) = Σ_i (−1)^i β(v_i) ω(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_{m+1}). In Simon's notation: ∂T(hω) − T(h dω) = T(dh ∧ ω) with dh = H♭ on M.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Lemma 4.5(2), from "we can write M = ⋃ M_j …" to identity (3) (chapter-06.txt lines 1200–1290, printed pp. 155–156). Simon mollifies h and writes ∂T(h^{(σ)}ω) = T(dh^{(σ)} ∧ ω) + T(h^{(σ)}dω). Since ξ orients T_xM, T(dh^{(σ)} ∧ ω) = ∫⟨ξ⌞∇^M h^{(σ)}, ω⟩. He passes to the limit with (1): "v·∇^M h^{(σ)} → v·∇^M h weakly in L²(μ_T) … since N_j is C¹ this follows fairly easily by approximating v by smooth functions and using the fact that h^{(σ)} converges to h uniformly". The printed argument is copied; (1) is proved on the C¹ pieces, as indicated there. Here ∇^M h is the approximate tangential gradient H of the hypothesis; on each piece it is identified with the chart gradient. Siblings used:
 - lipschitz_smoothing (cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing): Simon's h^{(σ)};
 - defect_identity (cmcs_cd_defect_identity): ∂T(gω) − T(g dω) = T(dg ∧ ω) for C^∞ g;
 - chart_pieces;
 - im_calculus (a), locality of approximate tangent spaces (TL).

Notation. N := m + 2; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; μ_T := R_T.measure = θH^N⌞M and μ_∂ := R_∂.measure = θ'H^{N−1}⌞M'. ‖α‖ is the operator norm of a covector; for a form β, ‖β‖_∞ := sup_x ‖β(x)‖. e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis, v♭ := innerSL ℝ v, and β∧α := alternatizeUncurryFin(β.smulRight α). K_ω := tsupport ω (compact).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) Orientation. For H^N-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM: by the field `orients` there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt N M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q, and Q = approxTangentPlane N M x by uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces. So ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ_1, …, τ_N) for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM, and |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖. The same holds for ξ' on M' (dimension N − 1).
 (b) Finiteness. θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^N < ∞ for compact K, so H^N(M ∩ K) < ∞. M is Borel and countably N-rectifiable. The same holds for R_∂.
 (c) Integrability. Let β be a continuous N-form vanishing off a compact K and b a bounded Borel function on K. Then x ↦ θ(x)b(x)ξ(x)(β(x)) is H^N⌞M-integrable and bounded by sup|b|·‖β‖_∞·θ1_K. Measurability: ξ is a.e. strongly measurable and evaluation is continuous bilinear. Likewise for R_∂ and (N−1)-forms.
 (d) Representation by measures. For every N-form ω̃ ∈ 𝒟^N, T(ω̃) = ∫_M θξ(ω̃) dH^N = ∫ ξ(ω̃) dμ_T: integration against the density θ, Mathlib `integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul` with θ as an ℝ≥0-valued density. Likewise ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ'(η) dμ_∂ for η ∈ 𝒟^{N−1}.

1. Smooth approximants (Simon's h^{(σ)}). By lipschitz_smoothing with σ := 1/(k+1) there are C^∞ functions h_k with ‖Dh_k(x)‖ ≤ K and |h_k(x) − h(x)| ≤ K/(k+1) for all x. So h_k is K-Lipschitz (mean value inequality) and h_k → h uniformly.

2. Leibniz for h_k (Simon: ∂T(h^{(σ)}ω) = T(dh^{(σ)}∧ω) + T(h^{(σ)}dω)). Apply defect_identity with U = ℝ^P, k = N − 1, μ = μ_T, ξ, μ' = μ_∂, ξ', g = h_k and η = ω (its hypotheses hold by 0(d)), and rewrite the integrals with 0(d):
 (i) ∫_{M'} θ'h_kξ'(ω) dH^{N−1} − ∫_M θh_kξ(dω) dH^N = ∫_M θξ(Dh_k ∧ ω) dH^N,
 where Dh_k(x) = fderiv ℝ h_k x and (Dh_k ∧ ω)(x) := Dh_k(x) ∧ ω(x). All integrands are integrable by 0(c).

3. The tangent field v (Simon's ξ⌞∇^M h, ω). For x ∈ M put v(x) := θ(x)Σ_{i=1}^P ξ(x)(e_i♭ ∧ ω(x)) e_i.
 - β ↦ β ∧ ω(x) is linear and β = Σ_i β(e_i)e_i♭ for every 1-covector β. Hence θ(x)ξ(x)(β ∧ ω(x)) = β(v(x)). In particular θξ(Dh_k ∧ ω) = Dh_k(x)(v(x)), and θξ(H♭ ∧ ω) = ⟨H(x), v(x)⟩.
 - v is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off K_ω, and |v| ≤ √P·N·‖ω‖_∞·θ1_{K_ω} a.e. on M, using ‖e_i♭ ∧ α‖ ≤ N‖α‖ (N terms of norm ≤ ‖α‖) and 0(a). So v ∈ L¹(H^N⌞M; ℝ^P) by 0(b).
 - v(x) ∈ T_xM for H^N-a.e. x ∈ M. If b ⊥ T_xM, then ⟨v(x), b⟩ = θξ(x)(b♭ ∧ ω(x)) = ±θ(b♭ ∧ ω(x))(τ_1, …, τ_N) = ±θΣ_i (−1)^{i−1}⟨b, τ_i⟩ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ̂_i, …, τ_N) = 0. So v(x) ∈ (T_xM^⊥)^⊥ = T_xM.

4. Weak convergence (Simon's (1)). Claim: for every w ∈ L¹(H^N⌞M; ℝ^P) with w(x) ∈ T_xM for H^N-a.e. x ∈ M,
 ∫_M Dh_k(x)(w(x)) dH^N → ∫_M ⟨H(x), w(x)⟩ dH^N.
 (a) Reduction to pieces. Apply chart_pieces to (M, h), obtaining ψ_j, V_j, Y_j, F_j with A_j := ψ_j(Y_j) disjoint, H^N(M ∖ ⋃_j A_j) = 0, h∘ψ_j = F_j on Y_j, and approximate tangent space B_{j,y}(ℝ^N) of M at ψ_j(y), where B_{j,y} := Dψ_j(y), for y ∈ Y_j. Note |Dh_k(x)(w(x))| ≤ K|w(x)|, |⟨H, w⟩| ≤ K|w|, and Σ_j ∫_{A_j} K|w| dH^N = ∫_M K|w| dH^N < ∞. By dominated convergence for series it suffices to show ∫_{A_j} Dh_k(w) → ∫_{A_j} ⟨H, w⟩ for each j. Fix j; write ψ := ψ_j, Y := Y_j, F := F_j, A := A_j, B_y := B_{j,y}.
 (b) H is the chart gradient on A.
  - Bi-Lipschitz chart. Let Ȳ := closure(Y), compact ⊆ V_j. There are 0 < m' ≤ Λ' with m'|a − b| ≤ |ψ(a) − ψ(b)| ≤ Λ'|a − b| for a, b ∈ Ȳ, and (ψ|_Ȳ)⁻¹ is continuous on ψ(Ȳ).
   Upper bound: mean value inequality on a closed ball containing Ȳ (ψ is C¹ on ℝ^N).
   Lower bound, by contradiction: if a_k ≠ b_k in Ȳ with |ψ(a_k) − ψ(b_k)| < k⁻¹|a_k − b_k|, pass to a subsequence with a_k → a, b_k → b, (a_k − b_k)/|a_k − b_k| → e. If a ≠ b, then ψ(a) = ψ(b), contradicting injectivity on V_j. If a = b, write ψ(a_k) − ψ(b_k) = ∫₀¹ Dψ(b_k + τ(a_k − b_k))(a_k − b_k) dτ on a closed ball around a inside V_j to get Dψ(a)e = 0, contradicting injectivity of Dψ(a).
   An injective continuous map on a compact set has a continuous inverse on its image.
  - Chart gradient. For y ∈ Y put g(ψ(y)) := B_y(B_y*B_y)⁻¹∇F(y). This is the vector of B_y(ℝ^N) with ⟨g(ψ(y)), B_ye⟩ = DF(y)e for all e. Moreover B_y(ℝ^N) = T_{ψ(y)}M = approxTangentPlane N M (ψ(y)), by step (a) and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (SimonGMT `HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`).
  - g is a classical gradient along A. Let x = ψ(y), y ∈ Y, and ε > 0. For y' ∈ Y: h(ψ(y')) − h(x) = F(y') − F(y) = DF(y)(y' − y) + o(|y' − y|), since h∘ψ = F on Y; and ⟨g(x), ψ(y') − x⟩ = ⟨g(x), B_y(y' − y)⟩ + o(|y' − y|) = DF(y)(y' − y) + o(|y' − y|). Since |y' − y| ≤ |ψ(y') − x|/m' and y' → y when ψ(y') → x, there is r₀ > 0 with |h(x') − h(x) − ⟨g(x), x' − x⟩| ≤ ε|x' − x| for every x' ∈ A ∩ B_{r₀}(x).
  - Tangent plane of A. By TL for the Borel pair A ⊆ M (M locally H^N-finite, step 0(b)): for H^N-a.e. x ∈ A, A and M have the same approximate tangent spaces at x. So A has approximate tangent space T_xM = B_y(ℝ^N) at x = ψ(y).
  - H along A. By hypothesis, for H^N-a.e. x ∈ A: H(x) ∈ T_xM, and r^{−N}H^N(E_r) → 0, where E_r := {x' ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : |h(x') − h(x) − ⟨H(x), x' − x⟩| > ε'|x' − x|}, for every ε' > 0.
  - Uniqueness along A. Let x = ψ(y) ∈ A be a point where the last two bullets hold, and suppose u := H(x) − g(x) ≠ 0. Then u ∈ T_xM. Put e := u/|u|, ε := |u|/8, and C := {x' : ⟨e, x' − x⟩ > ½|x' − x|}, an open cone with vertex x. Let r < r₀ (r₀ from the gradient bullet, for this ε) and x' ∈ A ∩ C ∩ B_r(x). Then |⟨u, x' − x⟩| > ½|u||x' − x| = 4ε|x' − x| and |h(x') − h(x) − ⟨g(x), x' − x⟩| ≤ ε|x' − x|, so |h(x') − h(x) − ⟨H(x), x' − x⟩| ≥ |⟨u, x' − x⟩| − ε|x' − x| > 3ε|x' − x|. Thus A ∩ C ∩ B_r(x) ⊆ E_r (with ε' := ε), and r^{−N}H^N(A ∩ C ∩ B_r(x)) → 0.
   On the other hand, choose φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, support in the open set (C − x) ∩ ball(0, 1), and φ(e/2) = 1. Since e/2 ∈ T_xM and φ > 0 on a relatively open neighbourhood of e/2 in T_xM, ∫_{T_xM} φ dH^N > 0. As η_{x,r} maps A ∩ C ∩ B_r(x) onto η_{x,r}(A) ∩ (C − x) ∩ ball(0, 1) and scales H^N by r^{−N}: r^{−N}H^N(A ∩ C ∩ B_r(x)) ≥ ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} φ dH^N → ∫_{T_xM} φ dH^N > 0. This is a contradiction.
   Hence H = g H^N-a.e. on A.
 (c) Transfer to the chart. By (b), ψ is bi-Lipschitz on Ȳ. J(y) := J(B_y) is continuous and positive on the compact Ȳ, hence bounded above and below by positive constants there. For a.e. y ∈ Y, w(ψ(y)) ∈ B_y(ℝ^N), since T_{ψ(y)}M = B_y(ℝ^N); here H^N-null subsets of A correspond to L^N-null subsets of Y because ψ is bi-Lipschitz on Ȳ. Write w(ψ(y)) = B_yŵ(y) with ŵ(y) := (B_y*B_y)⁻¹B_y*w(ψ(y)). Put Ŵ := 1_Y·J·ŵ. Then Ŵ ∈ L¹(ℝ^N; ℝ^N), because |ŵ(y)| ≤ c|w(ψ(y))| and ∫_Y |w∘ψ|J = ∫_A |w| dH^N < ∞ (area formula). By the weighted injective area formula (SimonGMT `weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative`, applied to positive and negative parts):
  ∫_A Dh_k(w) dH^N = ∫_Y Dh_k(ψ(y))(B_yŵ(y))J(y) dy = ∫ D(h_k∘ψ)(y)(Ŵ(y)) dy (chain rule; h_k and ψ are C¹), and
  ∫_A ⟨H, w⟩ dH^N = ∫_Y ⟨g(ψ(y)), B_yŵ(y)⟩J(y) dy = ∫ DF(y)(Ŵ(y)) dy (by (b) and the defining property of g).
 (d) Euclidean weak-* convergence. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V_j) with χ = 1 on an open O ⊇ closure(Y) (closure(Y) is compact ⊆ V_j). Put u_k := χ·(h_k∘ψ) and u := χ·(h∘ψ). ψ is Lipschitz on a closed ball containing the compact set supp χ (ψ is C¹ on ℝ^N; mean value inequality), and h_k, h are K-Lipschitz, so these functions are Lipschitz with a constant Λ'' independent of k, have support in supp χ, and u_k → u uniformly. Claim: ∫ Du_k(Ŵ) → ∫ Du(Ŵ), where Du is defined a.e. by Rademacher.
  - Let Φ : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be Lipschitz with compact support. By integration by parts for Lipschitz functions (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq`, applied with f := u_k, resp. u, g := Φ_i, v := e_i), ∫ ∂_iu_k·Φ_i = −∫ u_k·∂_iΦ_i. Here ∂_i denotes the line derivative in direction e_i, which equals D(·)e_i at points of differentiability (a.e., Rademacher), and ∂_iΦ_i is bounded with compact support. Since u_k → u uniformly, ∫ Du_k(Φ) = Σ_i ∫ ∂_iu_k·Φ_i = −Σ_i ∫ u_k·∂_iΦ_i → −Σ_i ∫ u·∂_iΦ_i = Σ_i ∫ ∂_iu·Φ_i = ∫ Du(Φ).
  - Density. Given δ > 0, first choose a continuous compactly supported Φ₀ with ∫|Ŵ − Φ₀| < δ/2 (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le`). Then mollify: Φ := Φ₀ ⋆ ρ with a smooth bump ρ of small support (Mathlib ContDiffBump, `HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left`). Φ is C^∞ with compact support, hence Lipschitz, and by uniform continuity of Φ₀ it is uniformly close to Φ₀ on a fixed compact set containing both supports, so ∫|Φ − Φ₀| < δ/2.
  - Then |∫ Du_k(Ŵ − Φ)| ≤ Λ''δ and |∫ Du(Ŵ − Φ)| ≤ Λ''δ, so limsup_k |∫ Du_k(Ŵ) − ∫ Du(Ŵ)| ≤ 2Λ''δ for every δ > 0, and the claim follows.
 (e) Identification. On O, u_k = h_k∘ψ and u = h∘ψ, so Du_k = D(h_k∘ψ) on Y. Also Du = DF at a.e. point of Y. Take a Lebesgue density point y of Y at which u is differentiable; a.e. point of Y is one (Mathlib `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div` and Rademacher). Let e be a unit vector. There are y_l ∈ Y with y_l → y and (y_l − y)/|y_l − y| → e: otherwise some truncated cone {y' : 0 < |y' − y| < δ, ⟨y' − y, e⟩ > (1 − δ)|y' − y|} misses Y, and since it fills a fixed fraction c_δ > 0 of every small ball B_r(y), the density of Y at y would be ≤ 1 − c_δ. As u − F vanishes on Y, D(u − F)(y)e = lim_l ((u − F)(y_l) − (u − F)(y))/|y_l − y| = 0. With (c) and (d): ∫_A Dh_k(w) = ∫ Du_k(Ŵ) → ∫ Du(Ŵ) = ∫ DF(Ŵ) = ∫_A ⟨H, w⟩. This proves the claim.

5. Passage to the limit in (i).
 - Left side. On K_ω, |h_k| ≤ sup_{K_ω}|h| + K. By dominated convergence (dominating functions (sup_{K_ω}|h| + K)θ'|ξ'(ω)| and (sup_{K_ω}|h| + K)θ|ξ(dω)|, integrable by 0(c)), the left side of (i) tends to ∫_{M'} θ'hξ'(ω) dH^{N−1} − ∫_M θhξ(dω) dH^N.
 - Right side. By step 3 it equals ∫_M Dh_k(v) dH^N. By step 4 with w := v (integrable and tangent a.e. by step 3), it tends to ∫_M ⟨H, v⟩ dH^N = ∫_M θξ(H♭ ∧ ω) dH^N (step 3).
 Equating the limits gives ∫_{M'} θ'hξ'(ω) dH^{m+1} − ∫_M θhξ(dω) dH^{m+2} = ∫_M θξ(H♭ ∧ ω) dH^{m+2}. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mollify h (lipschitz_smoothing): C^∞ h_k → h uniformly with ‖Dh_k‖ ≤ K.
Smooth Leibniz (defect_identity) for h_k: ∂T(h_kω) − T(h_k dω) = T(dh_k ∧ ω).
θξ(β∧ω) = β(v) for the integrable field v = θΣ_i ξ(e_i♭∧ω)e_i, which is tangent to M a.e. because ξ orients T_xM.

Weak convergence (Simon's (1)): on each piece of chart_pieces(M, h), H equals the chart gradient (uniqueness of approximate differentials), the area formula moves the integrals to ℝ^{n+1}, and gradients of uniformly convergent, uniformly Lipschitz functions converge weakly-* (integration by parts for Lipschitz functions, L¹-density).
Pass to the limit: dominated convergence on the h_k-terms, and step 4 with w = v on the derivative term.

subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, T ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) represented by the integer multiplicity triple R_T = (M, θ, ξ) (IMRep univ (m+2)), ∂T represented by R_∂ = (M', θ', ξ') (IMRep univ (m+1)), and f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz. Write Hᵏ = μHE[k], τ(R)(ω) := ∫_N φ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dH^{m+1} = R.action ω for a triple R = (N, φ, ζ), μ_R := R.measure = φH^{m+1}⌞N, and γ_{a,b}(s) := min{1, max{0, (b − s)/(b − a)}}. Then there is a family (R_t)_{t∈ℝ} of integer multiplicity triples in ℝ^P of dimension m+1 (Rs : ℝ → IMRep univ (m+1)) such that: (1) the carrier of R_t is contained in f⁻¹(t) for every t; (2) for every Borel W ⊆ ℝ^P, t ↦ μ_{R_t}(W) is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ μ_{R_t}(W) dt ≤ L·μ_{R_T}(W); (3) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P), s ↦ τ(R_s)(ω) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ; (4) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and all real a < b, ∫_a^b τ(R_s)(ω) ds = (b − a)·(∫_M θ γ_{a,b}(f) ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{m+2} − ∫_{M'} θ' γ_{a,b}(f) ⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{m+1}). For a.e. t, R_t is Simon's slice ⟨T, f, t⟩ = τ(M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t), θ, ξ⌞(∇^M f/|∇^M f|)) of 4.4, and (4) is the identity in the proof of 4.5(2) for the cut-off γ_{a,b} after the co-area formula 4.2.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 4.2, 4.3, Definition 4.4, the proof of Lemma 4.5(1), and the computation in the proof of 4.5(2) from (2)–(4) to "Using (3), (4) in (2), we thus deduce …" (chapter-06.txt lines 1197–1316, printed pp. 154–157). The printed proofs are copied. Simon's ε ↓ 0 step and his "countable dense set of ω" are the sibling of this node slice_identity. Here (4) is the averaged form of that step: Simon's cut-off is γ_{t−ε,t}, so b = t and a = t − ε. Siblings used:
 - coarea: Lemma 4.1, with G = ∇^M f;
 - lipschitz_leibniz: Simon's (1)–(3);
 - im_calculus (a): locality of approximate tangent spaces, TL.

Notation. n := m + 1, N := m + 2, Hᵏ := μHE[k], μ_T := R_T.measure. ‖α‖ is the operator norm of a covector; for a form ω, ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x ‖ω(x)‖ and K_ω := tsupport ω. v♭ := innerSL ℝ v, and β ∧ α := alternatizeUncurryFin(β.smulRight α), so (β∧α)(v₀, …, v_n) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i β(v_i)α(v₀, …, v̂_i, …, v_n).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) For H^N-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of T_xM := approxTangentPlane N M x: field `orients` and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (SimonGMT `HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`). Then:
  - for any orthonormal basis σ of T_xM, ξ(x)(β) = εβ(σ) for all N-covectors β, with a sign ε ∈ {±1} independent of β. Indeed ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ) for some orthonormal basis τ of T_xM (IsUnitOrientationOf). The restriction of β to (T_xM)^N is an alternating N-form on the N-dimensional T_xM, hence a multiple of the determinant in the basis σ (Mathlib `AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det`). So β(τ) = det_σ(τ)·β(σ), and det_σ(τ) = ±1 because the change of basis between two orthonormal bases is orthogonal;
  - |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖.
  The same holds for ξ' on M'.
 (b) θ ≥ 1 on M and μ_T(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^N < ∞ for compact K, so H^N(M ∩ K) < ∞. M is Borel and countably N-rectifiable; θ is measurable.
 (c) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H^N⌞M, so there is a Borel ξ₀ : ℝ^P → Λ_N(ℝ^P) with ξ₀ = ξ H^N-a.e. on M. Every H^N-null subset of M lies in a Borel H^N-null set (Mathlib `exists_measurable_superset_of_null`).
 (d) Integrability. Let β be a continuous N-form vanishing off a compact K and b a bounded Borel function. Then x ↦ θ(x)b(x)ξ(x)(β(x)) is H^N⌞M-integrable. It is a.e. strongly measurable (ξ a.e. strongly measurable, β continuous, evaluation continuous bilinear, θ and b measurable), and by (a) it is bounded by sup|b|·‖β‖_∞·θ1_K, whose integral is ≤ sup|b|·‖β‖_∞·μ_T(K) < ∞ by (b). Likewise for R_∂ and continuous (N−1)-forms.

1. The co-area data (Lemma 4.1). Apply coarea to (M, f, L) in dimension N = n + 1. This gives a Borel G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with |G| ≤ L and:
 - (A) for H^N-a.e. x ∈ M: T_xM exists, G(x) ∈ T_xM, and f is approximately differentiable along M at x with gradient G(x), in the sense of coarea (1);
 - (CF) for every Borel g ≥ 0: t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |G| g dH^N;
 - (SL) for a.e. t: M ∩ f⁻¹(t) is countably n-rectifiable, and for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹(t), G(x) ≠ 0 and M ∩ f⁻¹(t) has approximate tangent space T_xM ∩ G(x)^⊥ at x.

2. Null sets.
 (a) Let Z ⊆ M be a Borel H^N-null set containing every x ∈ M at which ξ(x) ≠ ξ₀(x), or ξ(x) is not a unit orientation of T_xM, or (A) fails. By (CF) with g := 1_Z: ∫_ℝ Hⁿ(Z ∩ f⁻¹(t)) dt = ∫_Z |G| dH^N = 0. So Hⁿ(Z ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = 0 for a.e. t.
 (b) G = 0 a.e. on level sets. For c ∈ ℝ, (CF) with g := 1_{f⁻¹(c)} gives ∫_M |G|1_{f=c} dH^N = ∫_ℝ Hⁿ(M ∩ f⁻¹(t) ∩ f⁻¹(c)) dt = 0, since the integrand vanishes for t ≠ c. So G = 0 H^N-a.e. on M ∩ f⁻¹(c).

3. Orientation of the slices (4.3). Let M₊ := M ∩ {G ≠ 0} (Borel) and ν := G/|G| on M₊. For x ∈ M₊ and n-covectors α put ζ(x)(α) := ξ₀(x)(ν(x)♭ ∧ α), and ζ(x) := 0 for x ∉ M₊. Then ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) is Borel. This is Simon's ξ⌞(∇^M f/|∇^M f|), with ⟨v⌞w, a⟩ = ⟨v, w ∧ a⟩.
 (a) Claim: if x ∈ M₊ ∖ Z, then ζ(x) is a unit orientation of Q'_x := T_xM ∩ ν(x)^⊥. Indeed G(x) ∈ T_xM by (A), so ν := ν(x) ∈ T_xM. Let τ_1, …, τ_n be an orthonormal basis of Q'_x; then (ν, τ_1, …, τ_n) is an orthonormal basis of T_xM. By 0(a), ξ(x)(β) = εβ(ν, τ_1, …, τ_n). Expanding the wedge, since ν♭(ν) = 1 and ν♭(τ_i) = 0:
  ζ(x)(α) = ε(ν♭∧α)(ν, τ_1, …, τ_n) = ε[ν♭(ν)α(τ_1, …, τ_n) + Σ_{i=1}^n (−1)^i ν♭(τ_i)α(ν, τ_1, …, τ̂_i, …, τ_n)] = εα(τ_1, …, τ_n).
  Note Q'_x = T_xM ⊓ (span G(x))^⊥.
 (b) For every x ∈ M ∖ Z and every n-covector α: ξ(x)(G(x)♭ ∧ α) = |G(x)|ζ(x)(α). On M₊ this is linearity of β ↦ β ∧ α, using ξ = ξ₀ off Z; where G(x) = 0 both sides vanish.
 (c) For x ∈ M₊ ∖ Z: |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖ν♭ ∧ α‖ ≤ N‖α‖ (N terms, each of norm ≤ ‖α‖); and by (a), |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ wherever ζ(x) is a unit orientation of an n-plane.

4. Good levels. Let G₁ be the set of t such that:
 - (SL) holds at t;
 - Hⁿ(Z ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = 0;
 - ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)∩closedBall(0,k)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ.
 The last condition holds for a.e. t by (CF) with g := θ1_{closedBall(0,k)}: ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)∩closedBall(0,k)} θ = ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,k)} |G|θ ≤ Lμ_T(closedBall(0, k)) < ∞. So G₁ has full L¹-measure (a countable intersection of full-measure sets).

5. The family (Definition 4.4).
 (a) For t ∈ G₁ let M_t := M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t) and R_t := (M_t, θ, ζ), with carrier M_t, multiplicity θ and orientation ζ. It is an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P of dimension n:
  - M_t is Borel;
  - M_t ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹(t) is countably n-rectifiable ((SL) and SimonGMT `CountablyRectifiable.mono`);
  - θ is measurable with θ > 0 on M_t ⊆ M;
  - for compact K ⊆ closedBall(0, k), ∫_{M_t∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)∩closedBall(0,k)} θ dHⁿ < ∞;
  - ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable (finite-dimensional target);
  - orientation (`orients`): by (SL), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹(t), G(x) ≠ 0 and M ∩ f⁻¹(t) has approximate tangent space Q'_x at x. In particular Hⁿ((M ∩ f⁻¹(t)) ∖ M_t) = 0. By TL (im_calculus (a), dimension n) for the Borel pair M_t ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹(t) (the latter locally Hⁿ-finite, since θ ≥ 1 and t ∈ G₁), M_t has the same approximate tangent spaces as M ∩ f⁻¹(t) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t. Since Hⁿ(Z ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = 0, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t we have x ∉ Z, so ζ(x) is a unit orientation of Q'_x by 3(a). Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t there is Q (= Q'_x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_t x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ x) Q.
 (b) For t ∉ G₁ let R_t be the empty triple (carrier ∅, multiplicity 1, orientation 0). It satisfies every field vacuously, since ∅ is countably n-rectifiable and integrals and a.e. statements over ∅ are trivial.
 (c) For t ∈ G₁: μ_{R_t}(W) = ∫_{M_t∩W} θ dHⁿ and τ(R_t)(ω) = ∫_{M_t} θζ(ω) dHⁿ. For t ∉ G₁ both are 0.

6. Conclusion (1). M_t ⊆ f⁻¹(t), and ∅ ⊆ f⁻¹(t).

7. Conclusion (2) (4.5(1)). Let W be Borel and g := θ1_W1_{M₊}, which is Borel and ≥ 0.
 - For t ∈ G₁, μ_{R_t}(W) = ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ.
 - By (CF), t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable; it agrees with t ↦ μ_{R_t}(W) on the full-measure set G₁. Hence t ↦ μ_{R_t}(W) is a.e.-measurable.
 - ∫_ℝ μ_{R_t}(W) dt = ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |G|θ1_W1_{M₊} dH^N ≤ L∫_{M∩W} θ dH^N = L·μ_T(W).

8. Conclusion (3). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) and put c := ‖ω‖_∞.
 - q := θ·ζ(ω)·1_{M₊} is Borel. For t ∈ G₁, |q| ≤ cθ1_{K_ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M_t (step 5(a) and 3(c)), so ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} q^± dHⁿ ≤ c∫_{M_t∩K_ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞.
 - For t ∈ G₁, τ(R_t)(ω) = ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} q⁺ dHⁿ − ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} q⁻ dHⁿ. By (CF) for q⁺ and q⁻, s ↦ τ(R_s)(ω) is a.e.-measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable on ℝ.
 - |τ(R_s)(ω)| ≤ c·μ_{R_s}(K_ω) for every s, so by step 7, ∫_ℝ |τ(R_s)(ω)| ds ≤ c·L·μ_T(K_ω) < ∞. Hence s ↦ τ(R_s)(ω) is integrable.

9. Conclusion (4) (proof of 4.5(2)). Fix ω and a < b. Put γ := γ_{a,b}, h := γ∘f, K := L/(b − a), and H(x) := −(b − a)⁻¹G(x) if a < f(x) < b, H(x) := 0 otherwise. Then h is K-Lipschitz (γ is (b−a)⁻¹-Lipschitz), H is Borel, and |H| ≤ K.
 (a) H is an approximate tangential gradient of h along M: the hypothesis of lipschitz_leibniz (Simon's chain rule (4): ∇^M h = γ'(f)∇^M f, with γ'(f) := 0 at the bad values, where ∇^M f = 0 a.e.). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z with G(x) = 0 if f(x) ∈ {a, b}; by step 2 these are H^N-a.e. points of M. Then T_xM exists and H(x) ∈ T_xM, being a multiple of G(x). Fix ε > 0. Write E(k, V, δ, r) := {y ∈ M ∩ B_r(x) : |k(y) − k(x) − ⟨V, y − x⟩| > δ|y − x|}.
  - If a < f(x) < b: choose r₁ > 0 with a < f < b on B_{r₁}(x). For y ∈ B_{r₁}(x), h(y) − h(x) − ⟨H(x), y − x⟩ = −(b − a)⁻¹[f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩]. So for r < r₁, E(h, H(x), ε, r) ⊆ E(f, G(x), (b − a)ε, r), whose measure is o(r^N) by (A).
  - If f(x) < a (resp. f(x) > b): h ≡ 1 (resp. h ≡ 0) on a ball around x and H(x) = 0, so E(h, H(x), ε, r) = ∅ for small r.
  - If f(x) ∈ {a, b}: G(x) = 0 = H(x), and |h(y) − h(x)| ≤ (b − a)⁻¹|f(y) − f(x)| = (b − a)⁻¹|f(y) − f(x) − ⟨G(x), y − x⟩|. So E(h, 0, ε, r) ⊆ E(f, G(x), (b − a)ε, r).
 (b) Leibniz (Simon's (2)–(3)). By lipschitz_leibniz (applied with T, R_T, R_∂, h, K, H) and linearity of v ↦ v♭ ∧ ω:
  ∫_{M'} θ'hξ'(ω) dHⁿ − ∫_M θhξ(dω) dH^N = ∫_M θξ(H♭ ∧ ω) dH^N = −(b − a)⁻¹∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θξ(G♭ ∧ ω) dH^N.
 (c) Co-area for the middle term (4.2). By 3(b), θξ(G♭ ∧ ω) = |G|θζ(ω) H^N-a.e. on M. Let q := θζ(ω)1_{a<f<b}1_{M₊}, a Borel function.
  - By 3(c), |q| ≤ Ncθ1_{K_ω} on M ∖ Z, so ∫_M |G||q| dH^N ≤ NcLμ_T(K_ω) < ∞.
  - For t ∈ G₁, |q| ≤ cθ1_{K_ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M_t (step 8), so the slice integrals below are finite.
  - Apply (CF) to q⁺ and q⁻ and subtract (all quantities finite): ∫_M |G|q dH^N = ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} q dHⁿ dt.
  - For t ∈ G₁: f ≡ t on M ∩ f⁻¹(t) and q = 0 off M₊, so ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} q dHⁿ = 1_{(a,b)}(t)∫_{M_t} θζ(ω) dHⁿ = 1_{(a,b)}(t)·τ(R_t)(ω).
  Hence ∫_{M∩{a<f<b}} θξ(G♭ ∧ ω) dH^N = ∫_M |G|q dH^N = ∫_a^b τ(R_t)(ω) dt. The last integral is an interval integral of an integrable function (step 8); G₁ has full measure.
 (d) Substituting (c) into (b) and multiplying by −(b − a):
  ∫_a^b τ(R_s)(ω) ds = (b − a)·(∫_M θhξ(dω) dH^N − ∫_{M'} θ'hξ'(ω) dHⁿ),
  with h(x) = γ(f(x)) = min{1, max{0, (b − f(x))/(b − a)}}. This is (4). ∎
proof_key_steps: coarea gives G = ∇^M f with |G| ≤ L, approximate differentiability (A), the co-area formula (CF) and the slice structure (SL).
Null sets: (CF) turns H^N-null subsets of M into Hⁿ-null slices for a.e. t, and gives G = 0 a.e. on each level set of f.
4.3: ζ := ξ₀⌞(G/|G|) is a unit orientation of T_xM ∩ G^⊥, and ξ(G♭∧α) = |G|ζ(α).
4.4: for good t, R_t := (M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t), θ, ζ) is an IMRep (rectifiable by (SL), orientation by (SL), TL and 4.3); otherwise the empty triple.
4.5(1): μ_{R_t}(W) = ∫_{M∩f⁻¹(t)} θ1_W1_{M₊}, so (CF) gives measurability and ∫ ≤ L μ_T(W); integrability of τ(R_s)(ω) likewise.
4.5(2) averaged: γ_{a,b}'(f)·G is an approximate tangential gradient of γ_{a,b}∘f; lipschitz_leibniz, then (CF) for θζ(ω)1_{a<f<b}, give ∫_a^b τ(R_s)(ω) ds = (b−a)(T(γ(f)dω) − ∂T(γ(f)ω)).

subproblems.title: From the averaged slice identity to the slice identity for a.e. t, simultaneously for all test forms (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 4.2 and the end of the proof of 4.5(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let R_T = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P of dimension m+2 (IMRep univ (m+2)), R_∂ = (M', θ', ξ') one of dimension m+1, (R_s)_{s∈ℝ} a family of integer multiplicity triples of dimension m+1 (Rs : ℝ → IMRep univ (m+1)), and f : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel. Write τ(R)(ω) := R.action ω = ∫_N φ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dH^{m+1} for R = (N, φ, ζ), Hᵏ = μHE[k], and γ_{a,b}(s) := min{1, max{0, (b − s)/(b − a)}}. Assume (i) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P), s ↦ τ(R_s)(ω) is locally integrable on ℝ; and (ii) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and all real a < b, ∫_a^b τ(R_s)(ω) ds = (b − a)·(∫_M θ γ_{a,b}(f)⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{m+2} − ∫_{M'} θ' γ_{a,b}(f)⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{m+1}). Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, simultaneously for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P): τ(R_t)(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{m+2} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{m+1}.
